Before attacking Japan, the focus
should be taken and completed for free manpower and civilian factories as well as to grant access to the focuses after it, since you cannot complete this focus when at war with Japan.

Once the war against Japan begins, Manchukuo should aim to rapidly conquer the Korean Peninsula and secure the coastline of Northern China as Japan is very likely to attempt to use the same strategy against Manchukuo as they would against Nationalist China; i.e. launching Naval Invasions and transferring troops across the South China Sea to open up new fronts. Whenever Manchukuo manages to conquer factories, these should immediately be put to use in expanding and improving the Manchu military to better oppose the Japanese. In addition to manufacturing new equipment to field new divisions, one could also improve their fighting capabilities by improving existing divisions and creating new division templates to improve combat performance and the Manchurian military can be further enhanced by manufacturing airplanes to field an airforce as achieving air superiority can be a very useful benefit when trying to conquer China as Manchukuo.

It is also worth noting that Manchukuo will remain at war with Nationalist China if they were at war when declaring independence, and therefore will have to defeat them as well. Unfortunately, in the latest version of Hearts of Iron 4 the peace deal that one would get by securing all mainland Japanese territory is broken forcing you to continue fighting Japan.

Not being given the white peace means it will be a continuous 3 way war and you will have to guard your ports from naval invasion, and should China be defeated first this will lead to a very messy situation as Japan will puppet China and some of the warlords. However this way you can easily defeat Japan using paratroopers since you still have access to Korea and you can take all of China earlier.

If you did not accept Japan's call to arms and thus managed to avoid war with the Nationalists and the Chinese Warlords, you can still join the Chinese United Front after completing the "War of Independence" focus. Provided that you managed to defeat the Japanese, you can leave the United Front and turn on your temporary allies. Doing this path you can take the focus to subjugate the warlords and get some of them to join you before going after China. However you will have to annex them manually before being able to take the focus to declare the Chinese Empire. It should be noted that whether the white peace triggers for the Chinese united front is random and may force restarts if you are playing in ironman mode.
When advancing into China, one should strive to launch spearhead offensives along railway lines to capture

to both disrupt enemy logistics and cause attrition to force them into falling back and to secure one's own supply. This is where having tanks can come in handy, as they make for excellent spearhead units. The coastal states of China have moderately more infrastructure and better supply lines than the interior states, which are underdeveloped and undersupplied, with little in the way of railways or supply hubs. Be prepared to build more railways as your units advance , building them in the direction towards existing supply lines and connecting them once they are secured under your control.

Once the Nationalists and Communists have been taken care of, Aisin Gioro Puyi now finds himself ruling over a country divided by warlordism, and in order to restore the Qing Dynasty and reclaim his position as Emperor of China, he must unite China once again by conquering the Warlords (
, as not only do these Warlords unlawfully occupy Chinese territory and have the ability to steal more of it through border wars, each warlord can also reform itself into a new
共产主义中国 through their National Focus Tree and contest the Qing dynasty's claim to the rulership of all of China.
Luckily, Manchukuo's National Focus tree contains all the necessary tools for uniting China. The National Focuses
serve to grant Manchukuo cores on all Chinese states and a wargoal against all Chinese warlords and the later National Focus

will grant wargoals against all other Chinese nations. Compared to Japan and Nationalist China, the warlords are considerably easier to conquer and should not post much of a challenge for Manchukuo. Once Manchukuo has successfully gained ownership and control of all Chinese core states, they can take the National Focus
Reclaim the Mandate of Heaven
and officially proclaim the restoration of the
清朝, thus restoring Aisin Gioro Puyi's rightful title of the Xuantong Emperor. As it reads on the lost Heirloom Seal of the Realm:
Shòumìng yú tiān jì shòu yǒngchāng
, "Having received the Mandate from Heaven, may the emperor lead a long and prosperous life."

After Manchukuo has successfully unified all of China under its rule and evolved into Qing China, they will have to spend some time recovering from the endeavor and rebuilding and developing China after decades of chaos and anarchy since the fall of the Qing Dynasty in 1911. A massive industrialization program must be launched, and this will involve the mass

of more factories and dockyards, the building of infrastructure and railways, establishment of air bases and naval bases as well as reorganizing and building up the imperial military to a modern standard, to defend the realm. Qing China needs to build a modern navy and airforce, and develop an army on par with that of other major powers, and possibly even venture into the realm of special projects. In many ways, Puyi's Imperial China will be embarking on a project similar to the Great Leap Forward initiated in our timeline's by Mao's Communist China , but Puyi's Imperial Revitalization has the potential to go much further and yield far greater results.

As far as industry is concerned, China's growth potential is roughly equivalent to the other great powers, with China being in possession of multiple core states with a fair number of building slots each, so there is plenty of room to build up industry in. When fully industrialized, China can easily reach over well 100 factories in total in just its own core states. When deciding which industrial format to choose, the preferred option here would be

, as once the industrialization is well underway, Qing China will be able to field a proper airforce to defend its airspace and the higher production bonuses for Concentrated Industry are more useful, alongside the bonus to factory capacity in states. When it comes to the Imperial Military, the Navy and Airforce are more or less and blank slate, as Manchukuo initially did not possess either, so Qing China can choose to build up its forces from the ground up according to its own design while utilizing the newest and best available technologies.

While this national reconstruction project is ongoing, one should also begin to look abroad and take stock of the situation. Depending on how long the reconquest and reunification of China took, the game will likely now be in the early 1940s, and World War II likely well underway. This gives Qing China many possible avenues of action .
They can decide to take the fight to
and conquer them once and for all, to finish off their most immediate and long-standing rival for good.
With Japan out of the way, there is nothing stopping Qing China from imitating Japan's efforts and replicating their efforts by launching and invasion and conquest of

and the broader Indo-Pacific region, to expel the Western powers from East- and South Asia and seize the region's resources for itself, reestablishing China's historical role as the regional hegemon. From there, China can proceed onward to Africa and the Middle East, and embark on an endeavour to carve out a colonial empire for itself. If the Europeans can do it, then Imperial China most certainly can do it as well.
印度 and create a collaborationist government out of them, and Qing China will then be in control of nearly half of the world's population.
nation, Qing China could decide to draw closer to

. A fully unified fascist Imperial China is as powerful as, if not potentially even more powerful than, Germany is, and can thus potentially turn the tide of the war in the Axis powers' favor by siding with them. As part of the Axis, Qing China may finally exact vengeance on its erstwhile humiliators and carve up the world according to its own designs.
Qing China can aid Germany by launching an invasion of the

from the east, to apply additional pressure on the Russians to bring about their collapse, allowing Operation Barbarossa to succeed, inflicting a death blow to global communism. From there, the Axis Powers can turn their attention toward the
Western Allies and focus their efforts on finally defeating them.
This time, the perpetrators of China's Century of Humiliation shall burn!

Alternatively, if still at peace with the Western Allies, then Qing China could decide to betray and backstab the Axis powers once Russia is conquered and seek to conquer them as well. This will open up the possibility of allying with the west while also being in a position to conquer all of Eastern Europe and possibly Central Europe as well, depending on how much of the Axis powers' territory China seizes compared to the Allies before the Axis are defeated.

As with any fascist nation playthrough, if one's ambitions know no bounds, then there is theoretically nothing stopping Imperial China from embarking on a quest to finally make the Emperor of China the ruler of "all under heaven" both in name and in reality. Essentially a world conquest, with China united, Russia conquered and either Allied or Axis territories secured as well, Imperial China will be well positioned to continue its meteoric rise, indiscriminately invading, conquering, seizing and subjugating whatever it desires, and reshaping the entire world in its image, creating a New World Order of its own. The Sinosphere shall become global; the new Sinic world shall encompass the whole world. The Emperor of China shall become the God-Emperor of Mankind!
Alternatively, Qing China could also instead decide to play it safe, by staying neutral, and focusing purely on building up itself and

fortifying/entrenching its position, potentially siding with the Allies if threatened. If played this way, then Imperial China would at long last succeed in bringing about an end to the Century of Humiliation and emerge from the war as an equal to the Western Powers. Additionally, if active enough in the war, then China could even have a chance to gain their share of the spoils and from there become one of the leading post-war great powers, potentially even putting Qing China on the path to becoming a possible future superpower, like China eventually did historically.

Be very careful about the border with China as a sufficient push from there can easily overwhelm the player without proper assistance from Japan. China's enormous manpower pool ensures that, should the player's military be sizable and well-equipped, China can simply outlast the player in a war of attrition.
China set aside, your next biggest threat is the

, as they have a National Focus that allows them to go to war with Japan and, knowing AI typical behavior, any Japanese puppet states are almost guaranteed to get dragged into this conflict and the Soviet Union is infamous for fielding large amounts of units. If Japan hasn't defeated all of its other enemies by this point, both of you will be in serious trouble.

When taking the focus to declare independence from Japan, try to time it such that it will finish either before the Soviets finish the Far East Fortification focus, or after they complete the following one: Operation Zet. Between these two focuses, the Soviets will garrison Manchukuo's northern border, and the Japanese will divert troops to this border in turn. Once Operation Zet is completed, however, and the Soviets withdraw, Japan will return the troops on your northern border to the Chinese front line, handily reducing the number of fronts the player will need to fight on and eliminating the need to divert resources to hunting the Japanese in the north before they can eat too far into you from behind once the Independence War focus is done.

To increase the chances of survival, Manchukuo should invest time and resources into fortifying its borders with land forts combined with anti-air emplacements. In order to maximize efficiency, you should build in layers. Queue up level 1 forts in every border province and, once those forts are completed, queue up upgrades to level 2 for every fort, and so on. Do not queue up a batch of level 10 right away as this makes each individual fort very time-consuming to build and slows down the entire project. Once you have built up forts, start constructing anti-air emplacements in every state. Forts will be of no use if the Soviets can dismantle them with an endless barrage of bombers.
Manchukuo starts off very weak economically, and it is required that Manchukuo focus on Industry and Electronic research early on alongside the associated National Focuses.

Although the player will likely be offered an invitation into the Chinese United Front, it is not recommended that they join, as doing so will make it so that Japan will only offer Nationalist China the offer to end the war. If they take the offer, the player will not receive any of the Chinese territory held by the Japanese after the White Peace is signed.

France has a focus to unlock decisions concerning whether to intervene in the Spanish Civil War, or encourage non-interference by other parties. If it opts to encourage non-interference, success will give it a stability boost. If it opts to interfere, however, it will unlock a series of decisions - said decisions will boost war support; after getting war support to a certain level, France can opt to intervene directly in the Spanish Civil War. By default, it can only intervene on the side of the Republicans, but should it change ideologies, France can instead opt to intervene on the side of the Nationalists, the Carlists, the Falangists, or the Communists. Interestingly, the way these decisions are coded makes it entirely possible for a Fascist France to intervene on the side of Republican Spain and also drag the Axis in.

If Germany goes down its historic tree, France can opt to mobilize in response to the remilitarization of the Rhineland . If the UK supports France, France will join the Allies, and if the Germans refuse to back down, when France goes to war, a civil war will break out. If the UK refuses to back up France, however, France can either opt to oppose Germany itself or it can back down. If Germany does back down in response to either instance, not only will the Rhineland remain demilitarized, but it will also give them a negative debuff that will lock off Anschluss for 1 year . Similarly, France can act differently in response to German demands for the Sudetenland than the UK; if the UK agrees to let Germany have the Sudetenland, France can either agree with the UK, which will also cancel its guarantee of Yugoslavia, or refuse to go along with the UK and form a faction with Czechoslovakia. However, if the UK refuses to let Germany have the Sudetenland, France can either opt to stay out of the conflict , or it can reaffirm its support . Similarly, if Germany overthrows Hitler and opts to restore the Kaiser, France can raise an objection to the Return of Kaiser Wilhelm II ; similar to the remilitarization of the Rhineland, the UK can opt to support or not support France, and Germany can either choose to continue ahead or compromise and instead install Wilhelm III as Kaiser. This will give them a similar debuff, but unlike the Rhineland Challenge Met debuff, none of Germany's focuses will be blocked.

If France is capitulated by a non-democratic Germany, and Germany is still at war with another major in the same faction as France, Germany can opt to set up an unofficial government in France - what government this is will depend on what ideology Germany is at the time. If Germany is Fascist, it will establish Vichy France. However, if Germany has restored the Kaiser, it will instead establish Bourbon France, although unlike what happens if France manually restores the monarchy, this Bourbon France will not have a king in charge . Alternatively, if France is Democratic and aligned with the UK , France can instead propose joining the two countries in the Franco-British Union - this decision will end the game for the French Player if the UK accepts, but in return, the British player will gain all existing French cores , all French Units, Ships, Generals, Admirals, and equipment; while the Union can remain afterwards if the British player opts not to let France go independent when the Union is at peace, they will lose all French cores and generals/admirals if they choose to do so.

Through the focus "The Blum-Violette Proposal", France can gain cores on Northern Algeria. Additionally, through the focus "French Union", France can gain cores on any of their colonies in Africa, the Middle East, or Indochina, although the cores gained will differ as the outcome is always random - interestingly, if Morocco, Algeria, or Tunisia was to form Andalusia, then be re-conquered by France, it can still agree to be cored through French Union, which would result in France gaining all cores that Morocco had , although this would be slightly redundant if Legitimist France was to do so, as Andalusia requires Spain and Portugal to be formed) - note that the Blum-Violette proposal would not grant France cores on Andalusia if formed this method, as said focus is fixed in regards to what cores it grants.

For your military, France's 18-width 'Division d'Infanterie' is good, though support anti-air is a good addition. The mountaineers and motorized infantry are also useful, but everything else can be converted to regular infantry. Medium tank divisions can be useful for encirclements but the limited military industry means you can't build more than a few armored divisions. A railway gun can be helpful for defending on the Belgian border and pushing back into Germany. Finally, building a lot of 1936 fighters is the only real counter to Germany's huge air force. The naval game isn't especially relevant as Germany is unable to construct a substantial surface fleet and Britain is capable of subduing the Regia Marina in the Mediterranean. As far as strategy goes, let your enemies attack without counterattacking, then push only when your troops are at full strength while your enemies are down to 75% or so.

Alsace-Lorraine has level 10 forts so the Germans can't make any progress against two infantry divisions per tile. This is a good route to take if the UK refuses to back you when Germany tries to remilitarize the Rhineland. You get a choice either to back down or to go to war against Germany alone. Choose to go to war. It seems like a disaster waiting to happen but it can work out quite well. The reason is that 1936 Germany can't break through a fully manned Maginot line, it is not yet allied with Italy, and it can't stage naval invasions, so you are quite safe from them. Put half of your remaining military on the Maginot line and use the other half to end the civil war. When it is won, follow the focuses toward "Little Entente". You are in for a couple of years with dismal stats but you won't be in any real danger. Eventually you will be able to start your own faction and invite into it, in quick succession, Czechoslovakia, Poland, Romania, the UK with its satellites, and Yugoslavia. Move all your forces except for the army guarding the Maginot line into Poland as soon as it joins. Germany will invade Czechoslovakia and may even force it to capitulate before the tide turns, Poland will be reluctant to join the war, but, once everyone is in, your combined forces will sweep through Germany east to west, very likely capitulating it before 1940.

France is quite possibly the best candidate to form the European Union as if staying democratic, it can expect to end up in a defensive war against both Germany and Italy, allowing both countries to be annexed in a single peace treaty. The main problem with forming the EU as France is the inability to annex Belgium, Netherlands, and Luxembourg but this can be worked around by going down the French Entente line in the focus tree. Be sure to kick Czechoslovakia out of the faction before Sudetenland as otherwise you will end up in a war with Germany too early. Wait for Germany to capitulate all the minors on the mainland before justifying on an axis member and joining the war.

Once the war starts its important to deny military access to all other belligerents and rack up massive war score on your own. The most straightforward approach would be to first neutralize Italy by launching naval invasions to encircle and destroy their troops before marching on Rome. Start in Sicily and work your way up the peninsula towards Rome. If you have land forts around level 6 or higher then the Axis nations will be very hesitant to assault your positions and you can focus on taking down Italy. Once Italy falls, be sure to quickly capitulate Germany before the Allies are able to do that. You need to have a high war score in order to pull off this strategy.

Once the Axis powers are defeated and the peace treaty commences, annex the BeNeLux countries in their entirety and as much of Italy and Germany in the first peace treaty as possible. Try to annex all coastal states as the Allies will not annex any states that they cannot reach. Only Italy's and Germany's starting regions are needed so a German Republic forming in Austria or an Italian Republic forming in Albania is very convenient if you can cut then off and stop them from getting more land in the peace deal.
An alternative way to form the EU is to allow Hungary to become a major power and then occupy and hold the territories needed before the peace deal.

If playing on multiplayer with a player-controlled Soviet Union, one method is to have them join the war and have them declare on the Benelux countries - as this will drag them into the Axis, they can be taken into the peace deal. Note that doing so may result in the UK guaranteeing them, so it's recommended that either the UK also be player-controlled, or the USSR have caused as little tension as possible .

Lastly, it is also possible to take advantage of several random events to increase Communist support high enough and flip France to communism, allowing them to manually justify war goals on Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands and annex them, then progress down the Democratic branch of the National Focus tree and drift back to Democracy and form the EU.

emerged from World War I on the side of the victorious Entente, having joined France and Britain in exchange for promises of substantial territorial gains. With the war's end, Italy had anticipated its promised reward would be commensurate with Italian losses in the Alps. However, at the 1919 Paris Peace Conference, the major powers,
, failed to honor most of these commitments. Italy received South Tyrol and Trieste, but Dalmatia was given to the newly formed

. Regions Italy had long considered as Italian, such as Corsica, Savoy, Nice, and Tunisia, remained under French control, and most former German colonies went to Britain. This perceived betrayal, known as the “Mutilated Victory,” fueled national resentment and contributed to the rise of Fascism.
Before entering World War II, Italy annexed

德国 by the Pact of Steel, it remained neutral until June 1940, joining the war to claim French territories such as Corsica, Savoy, and Nice. In 1941, Italy joined Germany and Hungary in the invasion of
, annexing most of coastal Dalmatia and nearby inland areas.
Aside from these successes, however, Italy's military performance was poor. Its forces failed to make significant gains in France before the armistice, suffered a disastrous defeat in

in late 1940, and botched an invasion of British Egypt, advancing briefly before being driven back in Operation Compass. By early 1943, the Allies had expelled Italy from Africa entirely. That summer, Allied forces invaded the Italian mainland, leading to Mussolini’s downfall and the collapse of his government.

Following the armistice with the Allies, Marshal Pietro Badoglio’s royal government saw much of Italy swiftly occupied by Germany. In the north, the Germans installed Mussolini as head of the puppet Italian Social Republic, based in the town of Salò between Milan and Venice. Badoglio and the king fled to Brindisi in the south without issuing orders to the army. The royal government, controlling southern Italy, declared war on Germany and claimed authority over the entire nation, sparking a brief but destructive civil war marked by partisan resistance. By spring 1945, with the war's end, Italy lost Istria and the city of Zadar to Yugoslavia, as well as all its African colonies. In the postwar years, Italy recovered and became a founding member of the
, Germany , and the Low Countries.

Italy is an interesting country to play despite being the weakest of all starting Majors. It is unique in that it is the only nation that starts off at war with another nation in 1936, that being

. Taking Ethiopia isn't a problem, but the war provides an easy early-game source of military experience for reformatting the Italian army divisions. Timing the end of the war is also important. End it too early and you likely will not be able to earn much experience for your generals and field marshals. End it too late and the war might just drain a large chunk of your manpower and/or equipment and the Spanish civil war might just start and end before you can finish the "

" national focus. While the Ethiopian war and Spanish civil war is ongoing, build up your military and industry, you will need them later. Some traits you may want to get with a small number of generals are Mountaineer, Desert Fox, Infantry Leader and Trickster, whilst getting them to level 6 if possible . With the pair of aforementioned terrain-based traits, you will be able to get the Adaptable trait, arguably one of the best that the game has to offer. Its 45% terrain penalty reduction makes attacking into finicky terrain that you'll inevitably have to fight through in a historical game much easier, and thus is very much advised to acquire whenever possible, not just when playing Italy.
After Ethiopia, Italy can decide not only the fate of the Allies, but also the Axis. In order for Italy to disrupt
, all Italy has to do in the beginning is to invade
before Anschluss and then attack

and then take Czechoslovakia after war with Yugoslavia. This can be difficult to pull off if Czechoslovakia fortifies, but successfully pulling it off will allow you to steal a lot of the low-hanging fruit that is normally meant for Germany, weakening them. Ironically, despite declaring war and making puppets from Austria, Czechoslovakia and Yugoslavia, this will still generate less world tension than what Germany can produce historically from taking aggressive action against said nations. From here, Italy can choose to expand its alliance by creating further puppets from

. One has to watch the world tension, however, as if it rises to 25% or higher, the allies will start guaranteeing nations you target, which can easily lead to nasty war with both nations. A war with both the French and British at this stage is likely going to be too much for Italy to handle, even with skilled play, so be careful.
That being said, sometimes Italy can take refuge in audacity. If world tension is below 80% and

hasn't joined the Allies yet through a focus, Italy could complete the national focus "Go After France" and strike them directly. France has a respectable military but Italy can relatively easily build up its own military to match them through superior units, though this might require stretching Italy's manpower pool somewhat. Be mindful, however, of the fact that France's military industry is horribly sloppy, at just 6 Military factories although, France's national focus tree can expand this quite a bit. If Italy builds up its military and industry , attacks France and manages to encircle and destroy enough units to cripple the French military, Italy could conceivably defeat France before 1940, allowing them to more than double their industrial potential if they annex France, or acquire a nice source of manpower if they puppet them.
From here, the path to supremacy lies open; Italy can either choose to strike at Germany or the United Kingdom and once those two are gone, the rest of Europe is within your reach. Only the

could theoretically present a threat to you anymore and that will most likely only become a factor towards the late game. Conquer enough land and you might just find yourself surpassing even Mussolini's wildest dreams and be able to restore the

If playing the more historical Axis alignment its worth noting that Italy is unique among the Axis of being within striking distance of the Middle East with its valuable and abundant Oil supplies. Using its North African holdings as a launching point and its ability to protect supply convoys through the Central and Eastern Mediterranean Italy is able to quickly seize not just the Suez but the entirety of the Allies Middle eastern territory. Just be sure to grab it all or else Vichy France will spawn and cut you off from further eastern expansion. Once this is done you are at your leisure to fabricate and push eastwards grabbing more Oil than you could possibly use from the weak Iraq and Iran. At this point you are then free to advance further into the British Raj and/or open up more fronts with the Soviet menace.

A robust and relatively straightforward strategy is to transition your military doctrine to "Superior Firepower" and deploy Support and Line Artillery in all of your divisions. In conjunction with fighters , close-air-support planes and field hospitals , it is possible to both attack and defend against most enemy units with relative ease. Once a reliable source of fuel and sufficient factories to support it have been obtained, the fielding of various types of tanks can commence. This allows for the further augmentation of breakthrough capabilities, enabling the breaking of stalemates and the encirclement of enemy units for destruction.

It is of the utmost importance to maintain a vigilant watch over the Italian coastline. Italy is a peninsular nation with a lengthy coastline, which presents a significant challenge when confronting a maritime adversary like Britain. Failure to adequately address this vulnerability could have dire consequences. To prevent a hostile power from launching a similar invasion of Italy, it is advisable to construct coastal forts at all naval bases and station units there to repel any potential invaders. It is also advisable to maintain a reserve force in close proximity to the coastal forts, in order to repel any attempted landings by enemy forces and prevent the encirclement and destruction of the coastal forts themselves.

As for your naval units, Italy is a peninsular nation so maintaining naval supremacy in the Mediterranean will go a long way to protecting against possible naval invasions . In the early game, when naval dockyards are in limited supply, a decent early-game fleet would be a mixture of torpedo-equipped destroyers and gun-carrying light cruisers , with some heavy cruisers added here and there as resources permit. These ships are decently powerful while also being decently expendable and replaceable. In theory, the light and heavy cruisers should engage and destroy enemy screening ships, allowing the destroyers to attack and destroy enemy capital ships once the screen ships are down. Once you acquire more naval dockyards, this combo can be further augmented with the addition of more heavy cruisers and even battleships for heavier ordnance. The Mediterranean sea is small enough that Naval Bombers operating from airfields in coastal states should have enough range to cover most sea zones, allowing you to support your navy. This also makes Aircraft Carrier battleships somewhat redundant early on.

When it comes to dealing with enemy submarines, one could set up specialized "scout fleets" consisting of destroyers optimized for detecting submarines and ordered to "Do not engage". These scout fleets can scout the Mediterranean for submarines and if they find any, they will alert the actual attack fleets, allowing them to make their way over and attack the enemy submarines, damaging and hopefully destroying them. If Italy wants to further assist their navy, they could build ships outfitted with minelayers and extensively mine the Mediterranean sea. Mines will cause enemy ships to suffer a speed penalty, making them move slower, which hampers everything from responding to and engaging your fleets, disengaging, and retreating from battles and fleeing from bad situations. Having enough friendly minefields around can allow the Italian navy to do a lot more risky/audacious maneuvers and get away with it, allowing them to punch above their weight against bigger enemies like the British Royal Navy and the French navy.
To avoid issues with fuel, Italy could invest in building fuel silos in peacetime and importing Oil to fill them up. If you manage to puppet

or any other nation that has a decent Oil reserve, you can import Oil at a discount. Once war does break out and fuel becomes harder to import, this can be remedied by occupying and/or annexing states that produce Oil. Alternatively, if conquering and/or importing Oil is not an available option, constructing synthetic fuel refineries can help address this. Just make sure to also protect these installations from enemy aggression as both fuel silos and oil refineries can be bombed by hostile planes and captured by enemy troops, so be careful.

allows the victors of a war to decide the post-war status of the losing

During a war, belligerents on both sides accumulate war participation, a percentage that represents the relative contribution they make to their side of the war. The capitulation or conditional surrender of one side ends the war, computes the
of each victor based on their war participation, and opens the peace conference interface.
The conference takes place over a series of

. War score is distributed at the beginning of the conference if there is just one victor, or over the first five turns if there are multiple victors. During each turn, all victors may simultaneously select and submit demands for 州 or 舰船. If multiple victors submit conflicting demands, a
results and the victors may continue contesting it on subsequent turns until all but one have forfeited.
Each demand involves the following roles:
– The victor making the demand.
– The country that will end up as the new owner of the demand. This is often the same as the negotiator, unless the demand is on behalf of another victor or is a demand type that results in a
, liberated country, or forced change of government.
– The country that loses the demanded state.
The cost of each demand is influenced by a variety of factors, including the type of demand, the value of the demanded state, the negotiator’s
, whether the beneficiary has a

or claim on the demand, proximity of the demand to states owned by the negotiator, and whether another victor is already making a demand or contest on it. War score is a finite resource, so the player will often be forced to prioritize those demands that are most valuable to them.
The conference ends when all victors exit the conference, typically after all war score has been expended.
The peace conference interface consists of the following sections.
Score and turn panel with war score tooltip.

The top part of the peace conference interface displays world tension effects resulting from selected demands and the player’s currently available war score. Below the current war score is the current conference turn. To the right of this value is the war score that will be issued to the player at the start of the next turn and how many turns remain to issue the remaining war score.
Hovering over the war score values provides a tooltip summarizing the total war score the player is entitled to, including what is currently available and what they will receive in future turns.
The Make Demands panel provides controls to select the following demand types:

Take State demands – Annexes the selected state to the negotiator’s country. The player also has the option to select a different victor as beneficiary of the annexation by selecting its country tile in the Current Demands panel.

Liberate demands – Liberates the selected state to the country that has a core or claim on it based on game scripting. If the receiving country does not exist, it will be created. Its ideology will be the ideology of its original tag, unless it changes during the game, in which case it will be its last ideology before becoming
Puppet demands – Creates a puppet with the selected state or adds it to an existing puppet subject to the negotiator, if applicable. Democratic negotiators can only create
Change Government demands – Creates an independent country from the selected state, but its government will have the same ideology as the negotiator’s.
Take Navy demands – Acquires the defeated country’s
. Individual screening ships are not listed; instead, a proportional number of the loser’s screening ships are automatically included with the demand for each capital ship.
Add Demilitarized Zone demands – Prohibits positioning military forces in the selected state for five years.
Add Resource Rights demands – Makes the state’s

available to the negotiator for five years. The resources depicted for each state on the map reflect the potential resources after upgrades and may appear higher than what will initially be received upon conclusion of the conference.
Add Reparation demands – Provides half of the state’s current
to the negotiator for five years.
Add Dismantle Military Industry demands – Removes the state’s
, degrading the defeated country’s ability to manufacture weapons.
The DMZ, Resource Rights, Reparation, and Dismantle Military Industry options are available only in conjunction with puppet or change government demands.
Demands list with country tile expanded.
Selecting a demand type lists the demands available for the selected type, grouping them under

. Country tiles represent either the defeated countries when take state or take navy types are selected, or subject/breakaway countries that will result when puppet, liberate, or change government types are selected. Green flag and red flag icons on each country tile provide an at-a-glance number of uncontested and contested demands for the associated country.

Selecting a tile expands the list of demands available under the country. Hovering over each demand displays a tooltip with more details of the demand, including its costs, beneficiary country, puppet type that will be created, other countries contesting, world tension effects, etc. Holding the
key during this hover will display expanded details on the cost modifiers of the demand. Once bidding starts, small country flags on each demand indicate which countries are bidding on it.
Selecting a demand will add it as an
in the Current Demands panel and will deduct the associated demand costs from the available war score. Clicking the demand again will cancel the un-submitted demand, refunding the war score.
Selections in the Make Demands panel are added in the Current Demands panel on the right side of the interface, which consists of the Victors list and Beneficiaries list.
Victors list with country tile expanded.

The Victors list is displayed by default and lists selected demands, grouping them under country tiles. Each country tile displays the country’s name, available war score, number of uncontested and contested demands, and war participation percentage. Selecting a country tile makes it the beneficiary of take state demands. By default, the player’s country tile is selected until another tile is selected. The current beneficiary is indicated with horizontal yellow bars.

Selecting the yellow arrow on the right side of each tile expands the list of current demands made by or for that country. Within the list, un-submitted demands are bracketed with yellow chevrons prior to the end of turn submission. Clicking an un-submitted demand will cancel it and refund any points that were deducted from the player’s war score. After the turn, if the demands go uncontested, the chevrons are removed, indicating that the demands are now submitted.

The remainder of each country’s demands list shows submitted demands from previous turns organized by loser and demand type. Victors cannot cancel their submitted demands from a previous turn unless another victor decides to contest it. When a victor leaves the conference, a green checkmark appears in its country tile.

Selecting the Beneficiaries button switches to the Beneficiaries list, displaying puppets and liberated countries that receive states from puppet and liberate demands made by the victors. This list is read-only and these countries cannot be directly selected in this panel as beneficiaries. Rather, their beneficiary status for a given state is determined by the available demands under their country tile in the Make Demands panel.

At the center of the interface, the map graphically represents the current status of different states during the conference, provides information based on selected demand types, and allows the player to select or deselect demands on states similar to the Make Demands and Current Demands panel. Hovering over a state displays a tooltip with demand information based on the currently selected demand type. This includes a breakdown of the costs. Holding the
key during this hover will display expanded details on the cost modifiers of the demand.
Interactive map and demand tooltip with expanded details .

The map updates based on the currently selected demand type from the Make Demands panel. States that are eligible for the selected demand type and affordable to the player will be highlighted green. If the state is not affordable with the current war score, it loses its green highlighting. On selecting a demand, the associated state is highlighted blue. On subsequent turns, if the state has been successfully demanded without contest, it changes its base color to that of the new owner. If a state is contested, it is highlighted red.
Each state has an information card displayed on it with the following information:
Flags of countries bidding on the state during the conference
A green flag to represent if the state has been demanded without contest
A red flag to represent if the state is being contested

If another victor submits the same demand as the player, on the next turn the war score spent on the demand is refunded and the Contested Demands window will display. The Contested Demands window displays the total number of contested demands, the total war score refunded, and a list of the contested demands.

The information displayed for each demand includes the new cost to contest it, the type of demand and name of the state or ship, and the countries involved in the contest. Hovering over a contested demand displays a tooltip with additional information, including details on other victors' demands. The player can individually select demands from the list to take action on or use the Select All button.

Selecting Close will close the Contested Demands window without making a decision. The Submit Demands button will be relabeled Contested Bids, and selecting it will prompt the player with the Contested Demands window to make a decision before ending the turn.
Selecting Forfeit will give up on the selected demands, allowing the player to keep the refunded war score. Selecting Demand will continue contesting the selected demands.
The decisions made in this window do not prevent the player from subsequently selecting or deselecting the same demands from the conference interface prior to ending the turn.

The Reset button, located at the bottom of the Make Demands panel, enables the player to cancel all unsubmitted demands within the current turn, thereby returning the war score to its original value. It should be noted that this button has no effect on any demands that have already been submitted in a previous turn.

The button labelled "Submit Demands", located at the bottom of the panel displaying the player's current demands, serves to submit all un-submitted demands and conclude the current turn. In the event that the player is unable to meet the financial obligations associated with the selected demands, this button will become inoperable. In the event that demands are contested, the Submit Demands button will change to the Contested Demands button. This will remain in effect until the player has determined an appropriate course of action within the Contested Demands window.

The Confirm and Exit button signifies the conclusion of the conference for the player and the closure of the peace conference interface. The button is only available when there are no longer any unsubmitted demands in the Current Demands list. Upon selecting the Confirm and Exit button, a warning is displayed, urging the player to ascertain that all requisite actions pertaining to the peace conference have been completed prior to exiting.

During each turn, all victors in the conference get to make demands simultaneously. Players make demands either on their own behalf or on another victor’s behalf by selecting the victor’s country tile from the Current Demands panel. If making demands on another’s behalf, only the take states type may be selected.

The turn ends when each participant submits their demands; in the player’s case, this occurs upon selecting the Submit Demands button. At the end of each turn, the game evaluates all demands to determine if there are any contests. Demands submitted by only one victor are considered uncontested and are essentially granted to that victor until another victor decides to select that demand in a future turn or until the conference ends.

If multiple participants make demands on the same state or ship, such demands become contested. The player is refunded the war score spent on any contested demands and presented with the Contested Demands window. The player can decide to continue contesting selected demands at an increased cost, at which point the refunded war score goes back into the contest.

If the player decides to forfeit, they keep the refunded war score. The amount of war score refunded depends on how many turns the demand has been contested, with the score fully refunded on the first turn of contesting, but on each subsequent turn, this refund is reduced by 8% down to a low of 76%.

Demand costs for each state are computed by multiplying the state’s value by various modifiers. Costs will vary between victors for a particular demand due to the victor's characteristics, the defeated state's characteristics, and demands already made on the state. The cost cap for any single demand is 9999 points.

Modifiers are factors multiplied against the state value to either increase or decrease the total cost. Factors less than 1.0 will decrease the cost, while factors greater than 1.0 will increase the cost. Thus, a modifier of 1.2 represents a 20% increase while a modifier of 0.8 represents a 20% decrease. The

It is possible for defeated countries to survive the conference. This typically occurs if the victors collectively fail to demand all states of the losers. Annexed states will be in an occupied status unless they are a core of their new owners; compliance gained during long-term occupation or through collaboration missions will remain in effect after the conference. Countries that have been forced to change government will tend to have poor opinion of the winners, while liberated countries will tend to have a good opinion.

The AI employs a complex set of generic and country-specific rules when weighing its desire to make demands on states. A high-level summary of generic AI behavior in the peace conference is provided below.
The AI will have a higher desire to make demands on:
Its own cores and claims
States that are next to states it controls
Allies' cores and claims on behalf of said allies
States that are taken from a country with different ideology
Demand types that are aligned with its ideology
Fascists and Non-Aligned will tend to annex
Democrats will tend to liberate or change government
Communists will tend to puppet
The AI will have a lower desire to make demands on:
Cores of countries liberated in an earlier turn
States that are already demanded by other countries
States that are occupied by a human player
Demands that would benefit a country of a different ideology
States outside of its influence, except for the following:
Specific states when taker is European
AI allies' claims prior to turn 12

In all cases, if the AI has a net 0 or less desire on a state, it will not make demands on it, even if it has the war score to do so. Puppets will generally not make demands at all unless it is on their own cores and claims, or on behalf of their overlord/allies for their cores and claims. The AI has not been observed demanding ships.

In the event a contest between AI negotiators extends beyond two turns, a tie breaker function compares each negotiator's remaining war score, influence distance to the demanded state, and country score. As these factors are weighed evenly, the negotiator with the greater average of these factors is more likely to win the tie breaker.

The peace conference’s complex mechanics make it impossible to provide comprehensive guidelines for every scenario; however, the following techniques may prove useful depending on the makeup of the conference.

AI victors can be unpredictable in contests and AI puppets are particularly wasteful of war score. If an AI ally is not essential for defeating an enemy, keeping them out of the war will go a long way toward giving the player more control of the conference and ensure all states are properly dispositioned .

Land combat damage and occupation tend to be the largest factors in war participation gain. Becoming proficient in combat will have a second-order effect of increasing war score in these areas. Naval and air combat are also excellent contributors for countries that can field an adequate navy and air force. Lend lease tends give the least return on investment and should be avoided when the materiel could be put to better use in the player’s military.

For non-democratic nations, collaboration governments created through the espionage mechanics allow the player to take advantage of the Compliance cost modifier. This often requires performing two collaboration missions, so the player must weigh their cost versus benefit.

Players should generally prioritize deciding the fate of states before selecting naval vessels and other demands. This is because the total war score distribution computed at the beginning of the conference is based on state value and does not account for naval vessels or the value of additional demands such as DMZs, war reparations, and resources. Even in a single-victor conference where there is no AI to contend with, the player may not have sufficient war score to disposition all states and take all naval vessels, particularly if the loser has a large navy.

If multiple contests erupt with the AI, it is worth sticking to demands for only one or two turns. This is because the player will start permanently losing some war score after the first turn of the contest and will incur opportunity costs on demanding other states. When there are multiple states contested, the AI will start forfeiting some of their demands at a rate of 1 or 2 per turn, but eventually the AI will stubbornly stick to a few demands and the player will face diminishing returns fighting for them.
The player may take advantage of two powerful cost modifiers during the conference to decrease cumulative demand costs:

Continuous political action – Once the player makes a puppet or force government demand on a loser, all puppet and force government demands on the same loser will be 15% cheaper on subsequent turns. This allows the player to puppet or force one cheap state on one turn, and then get discounts on more expensive states of the losing country on subsequent turns.

Influence – Demands on a state are cheaper when the player has control of states nearby, especially if they are on the border; this includes states the player successfully annexes during the conference regardless of how much they cost. This allows a player to annex a cheap state on one turn, and get a discount on more expensive states nearby on subsequent turns.

The effects of both modifiers are stackable for puppeting/forcing government actions. The player may, for example, annex a cheap state and puppet another cheap state on turn one, and then puppet additional states on subsequent turns with both modifiers multiplied by each other for a larger discount .

For single-victor conferences, these techniques will free up more war score for other demands . With no pressure from other victors, the player can use influence from annexations over a number of turns to work their way around the country, from cheapest to most expensive states, with significant cumulative savings by the time the last state is annexed.

For multi-victor conferences, the player can still benefit from these techniques but must balance the number of turns required to take advantage of it with the pressure that will come from competing victors.

There are two ways to come down on this path, but both converge on the Renounce the Treaty of Trianon focus; you can either choose to elect a Fascist king or you intervene economically outright. The "royal route" takes 5 focuses and the Economic Intervention only 3; however, while the shorter route makes it possible to complete 2 extra focuses, it also brings negative perks with it, while the longer route also brings stability and political power.

From this conjecture downwards, there is only one deviation; if you chose Economic Intervention, you'll have the possibility to access Renew the Protocols, Protect Austria and Alliance with Italy focuses. All of them have marginal impact, because by the time they would have any effect, Austria is annexed and the war has broken out. Nevertheless, they are good for cheese strategies and postwar games.
From this point on, it is mandatory to get rid of the armament restrictions , and do the Reaffirm Territorial Claims, to get more land, population and resources to feed the feeble army and economy.

The fundamental problem of Hungary is not so much the restrictions, but the dead end of its rearmament: there are simply not enough manpower, resources or civilian industry to make it a competitive player. The only resource Hungary has in abundance is aluminium, but without rubber or military factories, it can not be the source of a good air force at the beginning of the game.

There are two ways to expand: politically and militarily. Southern Slovakia is bringing in extra factories, core population and steel. However, Transcarpathia is labeled as a non-core province, and it siphons away a garrison force, while providing little benefits. In any case, Czechoslovakia usually cease to exist before it could be attacked, and it wouldn't worth to fight against the much better Czechoslovakian army for Eastern and Western Slovakia , and Germany would come for the rest of it anyway. Moreover, there is a later focus how to get the rest of the historical Upland anyway.

The next target is Transylvania, which is very strangely portrayed in the game. When you demand it and ask for arbitration, there are three possible outcomes: either the Romanians refuse , or they give you Northern Transylvania, or they give you the whole Transylvania.

While attacking and defeating the whole Romania might be a good choice for exceptionally good players, it must be noted that at this point, Romania has a much larger standing army and draws manpower from a much greater pool, while its industry is at least on par with that of Hungary. Moreover, even if this campaign can end in Hungarian victory, the only thing that would change strategically is that Hungary will have quite a lot of oil compared to its motorized forces before the war, and it will gain sea access.
If Romania gives Northern Transylvania, which is the most likely option, Hungary will have a few new factories, some more manpower, but nothing substantial.

To pull off a full transfer of Transylvania, Hungary needs the largest possible army on the border and good relations with the arbitrating nation. Plus, some luck, as RNG will ultimately decide it. Although it is much better logistics-wise, the real difference is in manpower.

The next area to look after is Yugoslavia, which is in many sense a far better prewar war target than Romania. First, it has critical resources that could substitute imports . Second, it is much easier to liberate the core provinces in it . Third, its army is most likely not stronger than that of Romania. Fourth, with the territorial concessions gained in Romania, it is much easier to defeat Yugoslavia. Fifth, if someone wants to recreate the historical silhouette of Greater Hungary in HOI4, Yugoslavia has to go down, while Romania is enough to be browbeated.
The political solution yields Vojvodina, but not even the West Banat, thus it is only good for a very safe playstyle.

The border with Yugoslavia is lacking supply hubs, thus it is complicated to field large armies there. Also the Drava river is shielding Slovenia and Croatia, thus the best direction to attack is towards Novi Sad and Pančova, where the terrain is mostly flat and not crossed by rivers. After taking these two regions, a concerted attack against Belgrade is recommended; by which time the Yugoslav resistance is about to collapse. If needed, a sweeping attack from Novi Sad towards Belgrade will collapse whatever left of the defenders.
From this point onwards, the player can decide how to utilize these early advantages. He can either join the Axis, join the Allies or stay out of the war altogether.

One last, interesting bit is the Claim Overlordship over Slovakia focus. When Germany is totally engaged in the war, and starts to lose, while Greater Hungary has grown into a force to be reckoned with, they usually yield them, at least as a puppet. From this point on, Hungary can either absorb Slovakia, or let it exist as a puppet state. It only has cosmetic significance.

With historical AI disabled, the fastest way is to invade Germany first. Head north, take the cities and annex Germany. This will get you two provinces closer. Next, invade France. In many ways, the USSR is the epicenter of Communist ideology, which finds itself at odds with many of their neighbors. With various territorial disputes with
to the west, and frequent border clashes with

Despite its large amount of manpower and natural resources, the country's stability is torn apart as a result of old power struggles and paranoia, with purges on a regular basis intended to root out all conspirators with often detrimental side effects to the efficiency of management, production and command. Their military is in need of rapid modernization in multiple aspects to keep up with their European neighbors. Russian Empire's collapse in the chaos of the 1917 revolutions and the ensuing civil war gave rise to the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics in 1922. Born from the Bolshevik victory over the White forces and foreign intervention, the new Soviet state emerged under the leadership of Vladimir Lenin and the Communist Party, committed to building a socialist society and spreading revolutionary ideology abroad. The early years were marked by economic hardship, reconstruction, and the suppression of political dissent.
Following Lenin’s death in 1924, Joseph Stalin gradually consolidated power, outmaneuvering rivals within the party. By the early 1930s, the

had embarked on a program of rapid industrialization and forced collectivization of agriculture, transforming the nation’s economic base at the cost of widespread famine, suffering, and political repression. The Great Purge of 1936–1938 further tightened Stalin’s grip, eliminating perceived enemies within the military, party, and intelligentsia, but leaving the Red Army weakened on the eve of global conflict.
In foreign affairs, the Soviet Union initially sought collective security against the rise of fascism, engaging in negotiations with the
. However, Western reluctance to commit to firm guarantees led Moscow to sign the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact with the
in August 1939, a non-aggression treaty that secretly divided Eastern Europe into spheres of influence. Following the pact, the USSR annexed eastern
, the Baltic states, and Bessarabia, and fought the Winter War against
, gaining territory but revealing serious deficiencies in its armed forces.

This uneasy arrangement with Germany ended abruptly on 22 June 1941, when the Wehrmacht launched Operation Barbarossa, the largest invasion in history. The Soviet Union, caught off guard, suffered devastating early losses but gradually halted the German advance through immense sacrifice and the mobilization of its vast resources. The turning points at Moscow, Stalingrad, and Kursk shifted the momentum, and by 1945 the Red Army had pushed deep into Eastern Europe, capturing Berlin in May. Victorious yet scarred by immense human and material losses, the Soviet Union emerged from the war as a superpower, dominating Eastern Europe and entering into a global rivalry with the
that would define the Cold War.

Each branch — army, navy and air — has its own "opposition support" value, raised by the focuses that align commanders and units to your cause. With no preparation it bottoms out at a 20% floor for that branch and is capped at 90%; the Stalinist SOS keeps the remainder.

Separately, the Opposition's popular support feeds a dynamic modifier , active for the whole war, that shifts the surrender surrender limit in the rebels' favour and against Stalin in proportion to that support.

The characters purged are always the same, unless a random purge already purged one of those characters earlier via the paranoia system, or if they are exiled. If the character was already purged, a random character will be picked. So the amount of people purged cannot be reduced.

With No Step Back released, one notable option available to players who stay communist is the ability to get rid of Stalin without a civil war if they go down the Right Opposition Path. However, this is very risky, since you need to assassinate Stalin before Beria becomes head of the NKVD, and should Paranoia get above 90, the civil war will fire. But if you want Russia to avoid another civil war, read on.

First, one should decide one thing: if they want to be cooperative with the Left Opposition, or if they wish to save the generals Stalin historically purges. This will determine focus order. Regardless, the first 3 focuses one should take are
The Need for Policy Changes
- for the political power you get, either hire Mikhail Kalinin or take Improved Worker Conditions for a much needed stability boost . After that, take
Gain Support from Party Members
, then go up to Partial Mobilization, and round it off with
Divert Attention Towards the Military
- while you might think that

is a good idea if not working with the Left Opposition, doing so will boost Paranoia, so it's best avoided. However, if you want to attack another country, consider holding off to see if you can go for War Economy instead of Partial Mobilization after justifying.
While this may seem like you will not finish the latter before the

finishes, the game will prioritize the player's focus as long as it completes on the same day . Additionally, if we take the focus that bypasses the aforementioned Center focus before, Stalin will merely speed up his focuses, whereas if we let it play out but not finish, he'll be on the same track but we'll be closer. While it might seem ideal to purge army officers because of how many you have, if you need to lower paranoia, focus on purging the navy - while you have more generals, the navy is not as important to the Soviet Union as it is to the British or Japanese. Generate new admirals as needed, and also forge production reports if you don't have the option to purge an admiral. Only purge officers if you have no other choice.

It should be noted that while Beria will be the one who can lock off the bloodless coup, if Yagoda is purged, he will be replaced with Nikolay Yezhov - this is both good and bad, since while doing so will significantly lower paranoia, Yezhov will generate more paranoia on a weekly basis than Yagoda does . The best case scenario would be Yagoda getting purged late , but as long as you can attempt to eliminate Stalin before Yezhov is purged, you're in the clear. Note that you can decline to purge Yezhov, but doing so will boost paranoia and cost you some political power.

Regardless, as soon as Plan for the Coup is finished, immediately click the decision to sway the head of the NKVD to your cause, and take
. It should finish before the NKVD head is swayed to your cause, so go straight for

, and clicking the decision to eliminate Stalin. You have an 80% chance of Stalin dying this way - consider disbanding the entire army beforehand if he survives, since you'll likely get a civil war afterwards. However, if he does die, congrats! But you're not out of the woods just yet - Lavrentiy Beria, who will replace Stalin, will continue down the Centre path, and should he finish

Return Democracy to the Party

One relatively easy way to deal with the Germany problem as the Soviet Union is to strike early and to strike hard. You start with nearly triple the manpower of Germany, though you have various debuffs and equipment shortages. Use your first political power to justify on Poland. Build military factories, run exercises to generate Army Experience, hire Chief of Army, switch to War Economy when your war support is over 50%. Update your infantry template to 9 infantry / 1 artillery + support artillery, engineers, recon, logistics. Disband units as necessary to put 80-ish fully equipped infantry divisions on the Polish border. Likewise, disband some of your mechanized divisions. Declare on Poland, then start justifying on Germany. If all goes well, you'll capitulate Germany by early 1938, earning you "We don't really like statistics", "The Revolution Triumphant" , a good shot at "Not a Step Back". Everyone will hate you , and the UK will guarantee any Democratic country you attempt to justify on after Germany, but you'll be out of immediate danger. You can immediately follow by justifying on Austria , and then either justifying or using the "Eradicate Western Fascism" focus to attack Italy for "The Pope? How many Divisions does he have?".

You must also consider the time needed to move divisions to China and back - in case you're planning to bum-rush elsewhere, or otherwise go to war with someone.

It's also possible to end Sino-Japanese war before 1941 by using volunteers. If Guanxi clique is at peace with Japan, it's unable to take *Demand Tonkinese Bases* focus, therefore Pearl Harbor never happens and USA doesn't join Allies, which will make further war with Allies easier. Japan will sign white peace with China if China controls all core states, Manchuria is capitulated and Korea isn't controlled by Japan.

To do this, support Guomintang and send 3 light tank, 3 mountaineer, a wing of fighters and a wing of tactical bombers early. Japanese divisions shouldn't be able to pierce even the basic Soviet light tank template. Prioritize clearing plains, landings, then supply hubs. Once Manchuria is reached, try to rush Mukden - it can be particularly difficult to take once China eats all the supply on that front.

However, its mountainous terrain, reasonable population, and starting forts provide a strong defensive position and a base from which it can expand its influence in China, with the potential to emerge as the underdog victor of the Chinese Civil War.

In 1912 following the Xinhai Revolution, the Qing Dynasty collapsed, and the Republic of China was formed. However, various warlords also arose, carving out territories from the former empire. In 1921, with the Western powers having ignored pleas for aid in confronting the warlords, the
answered by supporting both the Communist Party of China and the much larger Chinese nationalist Kuomintang government of the

. Under Soviet urging, the two sides formed the First United Front in 1923. In 1927, tensions between communists and nationalists flared, with left-wing KMT members either joining Mao Zedong's CPC or being purged by Chiang Kai-shek's right wing KMT. Soon, armed communist revolts erupted between both parties and the Ten Year Civil War began.

Nationalist campaigns into communist territory in southern China were interrupted from 1929 through 1931, when Japanese expansion into Manchuria and Northern China halted nationalist offenses for a time. Mao's forces declared independence as an otherwise unrecognized
existing in various pockets throughout China. 1932 to 1933 saw limited success for the KMT, though new failure to halt

forced demilitarization of the area around Beijing. But in 1934, careful encircling maneuvers crushed communist pockets, leading Mao's forces to exile on the Long March, nearly obliterating the communists in the process. However, the surviving communists reorganized in Yan'an in far northern China during 1935-1936. There, Mao's conviction in communism's inevitability strengthened. The civil war was temporarily halted in 1937 when

and the CPC and KMT formed the Second United Front to battle the Japanese, but almost immediately resumed after the latter's surrender, ending with the Republic of China's retreat to Taiwan and the establishment of the People's Republic of China under Mao on the mainland.

A new dawn in China
共产主义中国 finds itself in an equally precarious position as
China has to worry about its internal political stability, its unstable economy, its weak industry and military, hostile and opportunistic warlords and

that can threaten its holdings, it does have access to a satisfactory amount of manpower, has enough industrial capacity to mount a workable defense and can, with enough effort, execute enough reforms to stabilize its government and economy, build up its industry and military and secure its own territorial holdings and national sovereignty.

China on the other hand has equally pressing issues at hand; while the communists do not have have the same political and economic stability problems to worry about as the nationalists, they control very little territory, manpower, industry and material and are exhausted and crippled after the Long March and will therefore be hard-pressed to hold their own in a direct confrontation with the Nationalists, Japan or even other Chinese warlords. In addition to all that, Communist China also has a rather lofty "victory" condition to aim for: somehow, the communists must survive through the Chinese Civil War, take over all of China and repel Imperial Japan before they can consider themselves truly successful.
That being said, Communist China is not completely broken, for a cornered animal might just be the most dangerous animal, as the Nationalists will soon learn.
Communist China, unlike most other communist nations in the game, can actually decide what type of communism to adhere to:

national focus leads to a crossroads with paths to choose from. Each one allows the player to clean up the internal mess of the government and recover from the damage suffered in the Long March by seeking support from other sympathetic nations.

and the Comintern and having the two nations work together to spread the worker's revolution throughout the world. Electing this path will remove
from power and replace him with
. Joining the Comintern can be helpful for players who either are new to Communist China or wish to play it safe and do not want to risk facing

alone as if Communist China is able to join the Comintern, any attacks directed against then will also draw the Soviet Union into the fight. The Soviet Union is one of the more powerful nations in the game and being in an alliance with them will not only offer a great deal of protection from hostile anti-communist nations but will also guarantee that the Soviets won't antagonize Communist China as long as it remains in the alliance.

national focus and all focuses following it are based around the idea of creating an uniquely Chinese interpretation of Karl Marx's theories and having Communist China take matters into its own hands and conquer Nationalist China through using its own abilities and resources.

or any other warlord that decides to draw closer to the communists. This is the hardest path as Communist China will be taking on Nationalist China and Imperial Japan on its own. Communist China will have to take maximum advantage of everything they have available for use including things such like infiltrating nationalist territory and staging uprisings, starting border wars to occupy neighboring provinces and boosting communist party popularity in Nationalist China among other things.

A house divided against itself cannot stand

Electing to cooperate with the Nationalists will lead to the formation of a faction between Communist China and Nationalist China as well as demands for all Chinese warlords to join it, creating a unified coalition of Chinese nations to better oppose

. If Nationalist China decides to form the Chinese United Front on its own part, then Communist China can help provide more leverage by getting the Warlords to join the United Front as Nationalist China cannot do this by itself due to its focus tree lacking a national focus dedicated to that task while Communist China does have one. Once the Chinese United Front has been formed and all Chinese nations have joined it, Communist China will gain access to a repeatable decision that will, whenever it is taken, cause Japan and its puppets to suffer constant damage to their industry, infrastructure and even their army units, in hopes of provoking them into launching an attack.
The people shall stand up

Electing to oppose the Nationalists will unlock a number of decisions that allows Communist China to infiltrate Nationalist-held territories and stage uprisings, causing those territories to revert to Communist China's control. Communist China will also gain access to a national focus that will give it wargoals against its two neighbors,

西北三马, which can allow the communists to expand their holdings by a noticeable amount and gain space to build factories and infrastructure to better oppose the nationalists. These weak neighbors have few
provinces, so just bring some artillery support for an on-foot blitzkrieg onto their capital.
