are a feature in which a 国家, divided over

differences, breaks into two separate warring states, each with the goal of the complete annexation of the other. As long as the conditions are met, any country in the game may experience a civil war with any given ideologies pitted against each other.
during the pre-scripted Spanish Civil War.
Civil wars may occur based on the popular support for a certain

. If the support for a certain ideology that is not currently ruling in a country grows too large, they will start demanding a change of government. If the player ignores the clamor for reform or actively refuses to allow reform the chance of a civil war breaking out will grow. It will then start with an event allowing the player to choose their side. It is also possible for the growing ideology to start a coup, which would allow for a peaceful transition.

A country may influence ideological makeup of its own population by selecting the appropriate minister, this will result in an event in which they may choose between pushing internal support for a coup or popular support which will speed up the rate at which the ideology in question grows. Although choosing popular support does not make it impossible to have a coup committed, it does improve the chances of the civil war event firing before the coup. While a minister promoting a certain ideology is active, occasional events may occur that influence the ideological make-up of the country or add
that will speed up ideological conversion.
A country may also influence the ideological makeup of a another country by supporting it, using an

DLC, or a diplomatic action costing 政治点数 without the DLC. Other countries can do the same thing as well; this means civil wars may be actively pursued, but can happen even if not desired, if political support for a different ideology reaches high enough levels. Certain National Spirits and government ministers apply a percentage-based "Ideology Drift defense" stat to their country. This stat reduces the efficiency of ideology-boosting actions, which can reduce the chances of a civil war breaking out due to foreign ideology support.
Civil wars can also be triggered by foreign-funded attempted coups. For this, a country must conduct the relevant intelligence agency
or a diplomatic action costing 200 政治点数 without, and supply Infantry
. The amount of infantry equipment required appears to be a function of the target country's civilian population, with more equipment required for more populous countries.

Once a civil war breaks out, the country breaks into two separate entities. How it divides varies for non-scripted civil wars; the amount of land given to a side depends on the popular support for the ideology leading it. For this reason, for effective coups, it is recommended that the "Stage a coup" action is coupled with the "Boost party popularity", as increasing the support for an ideology higher will also increase the size of the break-away state. The two sides, the loyalists and the rebels, immediately enter a state of war with each other, fighting to unite the country under their flag. Once started, a civil war will act as a normal war with victory points eventually leading to capitulation as they fall. The only difference being that there are no occupation laws for occupied territory owned by the other side.

When the civil war starts, the country is split in two, in proportion either according to a pre-scripted event, or to relative support of warring factions. For example, the pre-scripted French Civil War is an 80%/20% split and the pre-scripted Soviet Civil War can be a 82%/18% split, a 70%/30% split or a 50%/50% split depending on the circumstances.
Divisions, ships, air forces, stockpiled equipment and divisions in training are split according to the percentage.
Both countries inherit all completed and in progress focuses and research.

The countries are not created equal though. One of them is considered the original, and another one the splinter nation. The original nation keeps its country tag even if it now has a different ideology and name, whereas the splinter nation gets a new tag.

The original nation gets to keep all hired political advisors as well as research and military staff. It also keeps all accumulated political power, army/navy/air xp, and unspent research bonuses. Generals and admirals are split in half or on party lines, depending on the country.

Civil wars can be influenced by foreign nations in many ways. The two most notable include sending volunteers and lend-leasing equipment. Once a civil war breaks out, the nation that supplied Infantry equipment for the rebels can offer further support by providing additional equipment through Lend-Lease. In addition to supplying basic things such like Infantry Equipment, a nation can also choose to provide advanced equipment like Tanks and/or Artillery for the rebels. This can allow the rebels to more effectively supply their military which can grant them an edge over their opponents.

Sending volunteers is another way to influence the progression of a civil war and can also be used to gain combat experience without actively joining the war. In order for a nation to be able to send volunteers to aid one side in a civil war, the sending nation must be at peace with the target side and must not be in a faction with the side they intend to support. In addition to that, the sending nation must have enough army divisions deployed to send volunteers.

The number of divisions that can be deployed is 1 division for every 20 active divisions . For example 176 active divisions means 8 divisions where 181 would mean 9 divisions could be deployed as volunteers. Note that a division with only 1 battalion in it counts as much as one that has 25. The minimum of 20 divisions with 1 infantry will enable 1 volunteer division to be sent. The sending country must have at least 30 divisions to send volunteers at all. Added to this is one division per 20 provinces in the destination country.

Historical civil wars usually occur when they did historically, currently the 西班牙内战 is the only example of this. In this case the division of the country is based on historical circumstances. Although pre-scripted, these civil wars may also be affected by foreign influence and support, volunteers and expeditionary forces, and may force other countries to intervene.
Civil wars can be incorporated into military strategy if one so chooses. A nation can choose to start a civil war in a another nation to weaken them prior to invading them. An example could be
德国 starting a civil war in the
to weaken the country before invading it.

However, one should be mindful that if a break-away state is fighting a civil war and its opponents are taken out by a foreign power, the break-away state will retain control of its initial territory while the foreign powers will only be able to make demands on the nation they targeted, due to them being separate entities. This means you will not be able to make any demands on territory controlled by the rebels once the peace conference starts, meaning that starting a civil war to safeguard an invasion turns the conquest into a two-stage affair. Invading and defeating the target nation first, then invading and defeating the rebels after that.
If, on the other hand, one needs to trigger a civil war within their own country for reasons such as changing ideology , then there are two ways that you can easily win a civil war.

If one is in charge of a small country : train a single cavalry or motorized unit, and disband all other units. Deploy the unit and have it take all the victory points. While it is possible that the AI will train units by that point, it will not stop you from winning with this strategy as long as you keep on moving the cavalry/motorized unit.

If one is in charge of a medium/large country : Get ahold of some army exp , and use that to design a template with a single artillery unit . Train multiple copies of that unit, disband your entire army, and deploy the trained units at the start of the civil war. After your forces are split, change the divisions you kept to a different template. Because the AI will never change the template, this will make their army incredibly weak, and also give you a large number of units .
In the case of the German Civil War, there are several additional strategies one can use to make it easier:

If one sends all the equipment they have in a lend-lease to another nation that is at war a day before the war fires , and cancels the lend-lease after the war starts, the player will have all their equipment.

If one conquers either Poland or Czechoslovakia beforehand , the borders will not adjust and the Nazis will not take any Polish/Czech territory; as such, the Nazis will be forced to use the troops they spawned to take the unoccupied lands, and leave the borders near where the Landstrumregiments you start with spawn unprotected. If you spawn units in Poland or Czechoslovakia, they can keep the Nazi Landstrumregiments occupied while you use your Landstrumregiments to secure the victory points.
In the case of the American Civil War, the strategies differ depending on if one goes fascist or communist, as this will drastically impact the borders.

If one is attempting to have the US become communist, the 13 states that broke away during the first civil war will break away; if one does not complete "Guarantee the American Dream" before hand, they will also lose the Midwest. As such, it is recommended that one beeline for said focus. Fortunately, you will not have your forces split when this war begins, so if you position your troops on the borders of the states that will break away, it will be very easy to move downwards and defeat them. Deploy some cavalry near Texas to secure the oil supplies - the capital can vary , but deploying 5 additional cavalry closest to where the capital is can help as well . Use your navy to ensure naval superiority on the East Coast and stop naval invasions.

The war to become fascist is much harder. Preparations beforehand can include converting the military factories in New England and the West Coast to Civilian Factories and taking the focus "Recruit the Free Corps" can help you deal with infantry losses. Taking "Work With the Bund" will prevent the Midwest from breaking free.

is typically used to represent a conflict between two sides, using a progress bar divided into distinct sections and decisions to push it towards some side for benefits. These are defined in
/Hearts of Iron IV/common/bop/*.txt

Each balance of power consists of 2 or more sides. While a balance of power can contain more than 2 sides, at any time the player may only see 2 which are chosen in the effect to initialise the balance of power.
To track the current balance, a single value is used, which can range from -1 to 1 with up to 3 decimal points. The
range is used for the left side,

is used for the right side. A side having power only has a cosmetic impact, changing the icon and the text used in scripted localisation. A side isn't inherently set as being left or right, instead it is assigned which side is on which half when the power balance is initialised.
Depending on the value, the country is placed in some range representing the exact degree of power on a certain side. This is usually used to grant certain

upon entering it. Most ranges are placed inside of sides, making it only possible to enter when that side is active. A range may also not be assigned to any side and be always visible, usually used for a single "balanced" range in the middle.

A range being assigned to a side only means that it'll be visible when the range is active, and a side may have ranges on both halves of the balance at the same time. Entering a range defined on a certain side does not necessitate that the balance is tipped in favour of that side. For example, if a side is set as a left side and yet it includes a range of
, then if the value is at 0.2, then the balance will be tipped towards the right side visually, but it will still be inside of that range.
A balance of power is tracked globally.

If 2 countries are assigned the same BoP, then the value of the balance will always be exactly the same between both countries. If both of these countries have modifiers pushing the BoP to some side daily or weekly, the effects of these modifiers will stack.

The French government was allowed to remain in power, but its effective jurisdiction was limited to the unoccupied "Free Zone" in southern France— constituting roughly 45% of France's pre-war metropolitan territory.

The Sichuan clique was a group of warlords in the warlord era in China. During the period from 1927 to 1938, Sichuan was in the hands of six warlords: Liu Wenhui, Liu Xiang, Yang Sen, Deng Xihou, He Zhaode, and Tian Songyao, with minor forces being Xiong Kewu and Lü Chao.

After the Qing dynasty's collapse, not one warlord had enough power to take on all the others at once, so many small battles occurred, pitting one warlord against another. The Sichuan Clique was divided into smaller warlord groups, or Defense Zones, separated from each other with distinct military, political, and economic boundaries. Large conflicts seldom developed, plotting and skirmishing characterized the Sichuanese political scene, and ephemeral coalitions and counter-coalitions emerged and vanished with equal rapidity.

However, Liu Xiang was the most influential of the Sichuan warlords. He controlled Chongqing and its surrounding areas. This region, sitting on the banks of the Yangtze river, was rich because of trade with provinces down river and therefore controlled much of the economic activity in Sichuan. From this position of strength, between 1930 and 1932 General Liu Wenhui and Liu Xiang improved their forces, organizing a small airforce and an armored car force.

In 1935 Liu Xiang ousted his uncle and rival warlord, Liu Wenhui, becoming Chairman of the Government of Sichuan Province with the support of Chiang Kai-shek. In the Second Sino-Japanese War, the Sichuan clique made a huge contribution to oppose the Japanese army.

The Sichuan Clique starts off with a decent amount of steel in China, and a few nations usually trade for those resources at the beginning of the game. The player can use the extra civilian factories to more effectively construct more factories or forts than the other warlords. Going down the industrial tree is very beneficial early in the game as it gives a research slot, as well as a civilian and a military factory, at that stage of the game boosting Sichuan Clique's industry significantly. As with smaller nations and China, generally produce only infantry equipment at the beginning, and then start a line of artillery for support artillery after making sure there is enough infantry equipment for the war. Construct forts along the northern border for land invasions, not to mention Sichuan Clique starts with mountainous forts in both the 1936 and 1939 start dates.

When allying with the Nationalists, as it is a good idea to first make sure the United Front forms, by forcing the Xi'an Incident . Once Japan invades, the player should help the AI defend the southern ports from Shanghai, and only sparingly send troops to the front lines. The troops of the front line should only be there to ensure the Japanese do not encircle half of the Nationalist army. After joining the republican government, the player should negotiate for support from the other warlords as soon as enough political power and/or army experience is accumulated. This ensures that the other warlords will not be able to join the republican government and threaten the player's ambitions to annex China. Depending on the strategy, it is actually good for the player to let the Japanese take the northern provinces. First, since after forming China, the player inherits all the Nationalist negative traits, it is a good idea to let the AI get rid of the Army Corruption/Army Reform decisions before building support in provinces. Second, the Nationalists lose support from every state they do not own, so after the Nationalists lose the northern provinces they should have around <30 support points. Sichuan Clique on the other hand, with the support of Yunnan, Xibei San Ma , and Shanxi, should have 20 support points. Now the player should focus on building support in two provinces that have the least support for the Nationalists, and once those two will support Li Zongren for the Premiership, it should be enough to take the

decision. Taking that decision will force the Nationalists to integrate their territory into Sichuan Clique, and the player will inherit control of the Nationalists' army, air force, and navy . After that, it will be a classic China game.

The Sichuan Clique can also very effectively use Border Conflicts to seize territory from western warlords starting with Yunnan and Nationalist states while the Nationalists are busy. One strategy is to focus on the west to keep the Nationalists between Sichuan Clique and the Japanese, but the Japanese also come down the coast so using Border Conflicts to occupy the southeast coast helps protect the core Sichuan Clique territories.

When making border conflicts, it is best to use divisions of 7 Infantry and 2 Artillery, as this will max out your combat width while providing overwhelming firepower. If you plan to drive Northeast, perform border conflicts with the Nationalists first. For the best results attack when the Nationalists are busy or about to go to war with Japan to gain land quickly. It is easier to attack Yunnan when the Sichuan Clique completely is bordering them in all Chinese provinces as they will always station divisions along the border, and then go with Guangxi and Guangdong to gain a bigger access in the sea.

If China capitulates, start a border conflict with any other warlords that border your clique, justify on Tibet if world tension is high enough to open a border with Sinkiang, there should already be a border with Xibei San Ma. Start a border clash with Sinkiang using the divisions listed above when Tibet is conquered. If the world tension is not high enough, start border conflict Xibei San Ma using the divisions listed above, start a border conflict with Sinkiang and take control of take all of their provinces. This process takes a long time, during this go down all possible focuses before Establish Rival Government, as some bonuses can only be gained through the base focus tree for Chinese Warlords.

If China does not capitulate or Japan does not go to war with China, continue border conflicts through China until most of it is owned by the Sichuan Clique. Begin conflicts with other warlords, completely conquer Xibei San Ma and Sinkiang first, Shanxi and Communist China are significantly harder due to the terrain and number of divisions. When Sichuan Clique borders Shanxi and Communist China on both sides, begin a border conflict with Shanxi first, do this until all of Shanxi's states are held by Sichuan Clique, start a final border conflict with Communist China, at this point it should not take long for them to fall, as Sichuan Clique should control most or all of China, excluding Mengkukuo and Manchukuo. This is a lengthy process, while doing this, complete all focuses possible before Establish Rival Government as some bonuses are only achievable through the base focus tree for Chinese Warlords.

When either of the above are completed build up the army, navy and air-force, due to control of a large amount of land this will make it far easier to produce equipment, boats and submarines, bombers and fighters. Move through the focus tree as normal. Conquer Japan, make them a puppet or annex Japan, annex Mengkukuo and Manchukuo, their land should be core states. This then leaves the Sichuan Clique with several choices; go to war the neighboring Soviet Union and Mongolia, go to war with the neighboring British Raj/Free France or go to war with another nation, this could be Oman, to gain a stronghold in the Middle East or Mexico, to then go through the Americas. Neither of this should be that difficult as Sichuan Clique now has control over most of China and Japan, when going to war with the USA, beware as they may join the Allies.

The Sichuan Clique should now dominate China and be the major power in Asia, with almost unlimited manpower and a large number of provinces to expand to, a world conquest is now within the realm of possibility.

The MIOs themselfes follow certain Archetypes from which they take the most or all of their traits. Most nations have special unique traits available in their specific MIOs. In game, MIOs have a name and a descriptor. That descripter is, in most cases, the name of their archetype.
Some MIOs have a descriptor that varies from the Archetype they are based from. Usually this is because they apply their traits to additional/different types of equipment.
Merchant and Escort Ship Builders
are the main source of a MIO's bonuses and modifiers.

All MIOs start with at least one trait that always confers some bonus to using it. Additional traits can be acquired by increasing a MIO's size, which add trait points to the MIO that can be spent on traits made available through the MIO's trait tree. Once a trait has been purchased, the purchase cannot be undone. When a MIO has at least one unspent trait point, players will receive a notification for it near the top of their screen.

The same MIO types across different countries will usually share the same starting traits and basic trait trees, but there are plenty of exceptions, especially in the form of unique unlockable MIO traits added onto a basic trait tree.

Like with 科技, traits in a MIO's trait tree can be mutually exclusive with other traits and/or have prerequisites . Some country-specific traits available only to MIOs of certain countries can also have additional prerequisites, usually that certain

MIO traits in the trait tree can be queued up by shift-clicking their icons instead of clicking them . When a MIO gains trait points , it will automatically attempt to spend them on available traits in its trait queue. The current trait queue for a MIO can be viewed by clicking the

button in the MIO trait tree interface. Queued traits can also be reordered through the interface made available through that button. They can also be dequeued either by clicking the X button next to them in the trait queue view or by shift-clicking their icons in the trait tree.

It can sometimes be a good idea to delay acquiring certain traits, potentially indefinitely, and leave trait points unspent. Some traits can apply maluses that outweight the benefits of their bonuses, so delaying them until their maluses have come less relevant can be a wise choice. Infantry equipment MIOs can be an especially common example of this, where the fairly minor breakthrough bonuses that come from some of their traits are often not worth the more substantial production cost maluses that come with those same traits.

Before the First World War,
was part of the Ottoman Empire. The Ottomans were defeated and driven from much of the area by the

during the dissolution of the Ottoman Empire. On 11 November 1920, Iraq became a League of Nations mandate under British control with the name "State of Iraq". The British installed the Hashemite king, Faisal I to govern the mandate. Britain would then grant independence to the Kingdom of Iraq in 1932, on the urging of King Faisal. King Ghazi ruled as a figurehead after King Faisal's death in 1933, while undermined by attempted military coups, until his death in 1939. Ghazi was followed by his underage son, Faisal II. 'Abd al-Ilah served as Regent during Faisal's minority.

On 1 April 1941, Rashid Ali al-Gaylani and members of the Golden Square staged a coup d'état and overthrew the government of 'Abd al-Ilah. During the subsequent Anglo-Iraqi War, the United Kingdom invaded Iraq for fear that the Rashid Ali government might cut oil supplies to Western nations because of his links to the Axis powers. The war started on the 2nd of May, and the British, defeated the forces of Al-Gaylani, forcing an armistice on the 31st of May.

A military occupation followed the restoration of the pre-coup government of the Hashemite monarchy. The occupation ended on 26 October 1947, although Britain was to retain military bases in Iraq until 1954. The rulers during the occupation and the remainder of the Hashemite monarchy were Nuri as-Said, the autocratic Prime Minister, who also ruled from 1930–1932, and 'Abd al-Ilah, the former Regent who now served as an adviser to King Faisal II.

Iraq is a small and hard nation to play as, although it does enjoy somewhat better stats above other Arab countries, having access to lots of oil and 3 provinces with building slots. Iraq is in a decent position to join the second world war and fight in Mesopotamia and North Africa and depending on which side of the war it joins, it can become an important support nation for an Axis advance into Africa and Mesopotamia, relieve pressure for the Allies in this region, or even provide the Comintern with a base in the middle east.

The first steps to take as Iraq is to go down the Industry Effort branch of the generic focus tree, which will give you access to essential civilian factories and Military factories. Iraq starts with an almost negligible industry so starting down this path early on is important, but if you are seeking to change your ideology then go down the political effort branch first. Technologically you should put a priority on the industrial tech section, as this will make better usage of what few currently existing factories you have and save you much needed time on building factories and producing equipment. Be sure to utilize decisions and conquered land to build more factories when you get the chance.

Militarily, for most of the game you will have to seek an infantry-based army as Iraq's industry is too small for mechanization or motorization. Tanks and heavy equipment should be avoided unless you build up a large industrial base of at least more than 12 military factories, and even then, it is best recommended to keep your army infantry based. When it comes to doctrines, Iraq's small manpower calls for the superior firepower branch in order to save manpower and make the most out of support equipment and artillery bonuses as this is most of the equipment you can spare producing besides infantry equipment.

Politically, you start as a non-aligned despotism, but unlike other Arab nations with a 20% fascist popularity, allowing you to turn fascist more quickly . You can only change your ideology through the generic method of utilizing advisors and going through a civil war or referendum, but in rare cases if Turkey goes down a fascist route, they may change you to fascist through a focus.
When it comes to World War 2,

with the historical focuses on you will not be attacked by another country. However, with historical focuses turned off you may be attacked by Britain, Turkey, or the Soviet Union through their unique focus trees. Geographically, Iraq is in a good position to take a major role in the middle eastern and north African theaters of the war, which can benefit either side to a good degree.

For the Axis, you can re-enforce Italy or Vichy France's soldiers in Syria and allow them to focus their manpower elsewhere by securing Syria and knocking out British forces in Kuwait . When fighting in this front you can tie up many British and free French forces in Syria and the Levant region, keeping them from more important campaigns in Europe and straining their supplies in the region. Eventually you can make your way down to Egypt and take the Suez Canal, further assisting Axis forces. But on the other hand, with the allies you can take off pressure on the allies in the region by quickly expelling Vichy forces from Syria and protect the region from Italian infantry that will occasionally enter through Lebanon or the Sinai. Whichever option you choose, you must remain aware of your limited industry, supply lines, and the superiority of foreign forces as you fight in World War 2.

The last battle with the Germans was clearly complacency and a mistake of our part, but the chance to restore the nation's honour shall not be missed. A naval invasion will surely go unnoticed. Prior to joining against Germany, use your navy and air force to assert total control on the Channel. At the same time, organize a few naval invasion spots. Land in Dunkirk and Cherbourg, and have a handful of troops at disposal. As the Channel supremacy is taken care of, the forces should land in a couple of coastal tiles. If successful, rush to sweep all the way down south until Paris is liberated. Then, take the fight to the Axis. Should the Vichy remain neutral even in this war, take almost all the bordering lands with Vichy and annex them by event, henceforth uniting the French lands and dissolving the Vichy Government.

The Dutch East Indies formally came into existence in January 1st 1800 when the Dutch government seized the assets of Dutch East India Company which had declared bankruptcy. After a short French and British interregnums during the Napoleonic Wars, the colony was returned to the Dutch rule and promptly expanded colonial rule in the archipelago, finally finished after the defeat of Atjeh rebels in 1912 and the conquest of Vogelkop in 1920.

Politically, the colony experienced a small, but continuous, reform since the implementation of Ethical Policies in 1901, which has resulted in formation of several political parties such as Indische Partij , Partai Nasional Indonesia , Partai Komunis Indonesia , and Partai Indonesia Raya . But flare-ups from revolutionary elements in the 1926 Communist Rebellion has significantly pushed back the reforms through a political crackdown which has lasted until 1935. Thus, the Volksraad that has been formed as a quasi-parliament for a future independent Indies government has also had its power significantly reduced compared to the Governor-General's. Furthermore, along with the Indonesian communists, the leaders of the nascent Indonesian nationalist movement has also jailed in the crackdown, such as Sukarno to the island of Flores and Mohammad Hatta and Sutan Syahrir to Boven-Digoel .

Economically, the colony is at a deep crisis, having its economy plummeted by De Malaise . Wages were being cut down and even the projects related to Ethical Policies were stopped to also helped bearing the economic burden from the
' own Crisisjaren. Exports such as oil, rubber, and cash crops were also plummeted with European and American markets fizzled out because of the ongoing crisis, with a new player,

has gaining more and more shares of both import and export markets from the East Indies. The Directory of Economic Affairs under the leadership of George Charles Hart and his vice-director Hubertus Johannes van Mook has mitigated De Malaise's worst effects by giving land grants to the village-oriented plantations and public ownership of communications and finance facilities as welfare measures to keep the populace calm, to the dismay of Dutch industrialists.

Reeling with the effects of the Malaise, inadequate military in both weaponry, manpower, and discipline, and also the reactionary colonial government maintaining its repressive power, the East Indies is at a crossroads in 1936.

The Dutch East Indies is one of the most resource-rich nations in the world. With massive room for industrial growth, the country faces a few problems: it is an Integrated Puppet of the Netherlands, it has several states that haven't been cored yet, the industry is small and lacking equipment. To break free, you have to increase your Autonomy from Integrated Puppet to Free. Fortunately, all it is not lost. And it doesn't have to rely on the grind, as the Dutch East Indies has a focus tree.
Strategy for Obtaining Independence Peacefully; TAOG

If you choose this path, you will need to build at least 15 Military Factories in order to produce any equipment at hand. Along with your civilian industry by 12 factories. Last but not least 10 Naval Dockyards. It is recommended to use the focuses of selling rubber in order to obtain Military Factories and Civilian Factories via Decisions. Be warned to not be too absorbed on selling rubber constantly as the reducing can be noticeable. Manually, it is also best to place Military Factories in Java, Sumatra, and the Lesser Sunda Islands, as these will be the easiest islands to defend against any foe and will ensure your control over at least two of them in a Civil War. Fortunately, it won't be the case. As working on the industry part goes steady, be sure to go with the negotiations event with the Volksraad. As the status quo or the early revolution can be more of a turmoil.

The player should begin the game by taking a few focuses that makes way for the independence, gradually increasing its autonomy and as well as improving the infrastructure. And, taking decisions of the Volksraad to increase the said autonomy faster, and to increase and flip to democracy as soon as possible. Arming our infantry with anti-tank rifles will allow them to take out lighter armored vehicles while maintaining mobility.
For infantry to effectively engage heavier armored units, high-explosive anti-tank weapons need to be made smaller and lighter.
Automatic weapons are becoming more portable. Submachine guns have already proven effective and the development of hand-held support weapons must continue.
The development of automatic weapons which combine the aspects of light and heavy machine guns allows versatility in how our infantry employ their equipment.
While maintaining and improving reliability of machine guns, we can also experiment with higher firing rates to ensure lethality of the constant stream of bullets.
With the increased use of assault rifles, developing automatic weapons that can be used in any environment by all soldiers is a priority for a modern army.
Being able to see the enemy without being seen is key to night operations. With the invention of infra-red technology, we can outfit our army with devices which, though unwieldy, make this possible.

Early infra-red scopes, although initially intended for use by snipers, had a limited vision range. As both the portability and vision improves, these devices can be used by more troops operating at night.
During the Great War the armies starting using basic civilian trucks for transporting supplies and hauling equipment. These have since become an integral part of most armies

Motorizing infantry is the first stage to mechanizing an army. Civilian trucks are readily adapted to military uses of transporting soldiers, towing guns, and carrying equipment and supplies. This greatly increases the strategic mobility of infantry units, which would otherwise rely on marching.

Multiple rocket launchers such as these deliver explosives to a target area more quickly than conventional artillery, but with lower accuracy and requiring a longer time to reload. Being mounted on trucks, this version is able to launch attacks and change positions before the enemy can return fire.

Mechanized infantry is infantry equipped with armored personnel carriers or infantry fighting vehicles for transport and combat. Mechanized infantry is distinguished from motorized infantry in that its vehicles provide a degree of protection from hostile fire, as opposed to soft-skinned wheeled vehicles for motorized infantry.

Amphibious Tractors, or Amtracs, allow Marines to be landed on a beach under armored protection. However, this comes at the cost of poor fuel efficiency.
These Amtracs feature several improvements over the base version, such as rear loading ramp for easier unloading on the beach.
. These are effectively weaker, softer, much faster, and slightly cheaper alternatives to
, respectively. In theory, their niche is would be for somewhat of a hybrid role between light tanks and motorized infantry, though players may struggle to find a practical use for this niche.
Where previous armored cars were simply commercial models with thin steel plating, this model was designed from the ground up to carry armor and light armament.
An improved internal layout and additional ammunition storage creates a more effective armored car.
Changes on the battlefield require a much heavier armament and thicker armor to defeat enemy light untis and survive to report back.
Our light mechanized units will come into contact with enemy tank forces at some point. Developing a special anti-tank variant would give them a fighting chance.

Troops specializing in amphibious warfare are growing ever more indispensable. Improvised methods and equipment become things of the past as our naval infantry is supported by specialized landing craft and training.
Amphibious warfare requires constant innovation. Improved logistical support and portable harbors can enable our marines to perform landings that may otherwise have been impossible.
Marines can be more than just amphibious infantry. In the future, our marine corps will be among the most disciplined and organized special forces.
Combat in mountain ranges exposes troops to many perils, but sometimes cannot be avoided. We can minimize these risks by providing our soldiers with specialized training for this environment.
Going beyond survival, our forces can be trained to use mountains to their advantage. With light equipment and mule transports, they can maneuver in this terrain better than other infantry.
Preparing for the most arduous mountain missions in high altitudes and low temperatures will require extraordinary training and discipline from our mountain troops.
By incorporating airborne forces into our army, we can make forced entries and position key troops in previously inaccessible areas, allowing for new tactical opportunities.

Transitioning from small operations with only a few paratroopers to larger airborne divisions paves way for massive airborne landings, taking these forces beyond a novelty to a natural part of warfare.

Learning to adapt paradrop operations according to weather, standardizing equipment such as jump boots and extended specialized training will minimize the confusion and risks involved in these dangerous missions.

From the late 17th century, the Omani Sultanate was a powerful empire, vying with Portugal and Britain for influence in the Persian Gulf and Indian Ocean. At its peak in the 19th century, Omani influence or control extended across the Strait of Hormuz to modern-day Iran and Pakistan, and as far south as Zanzibar . As its power declined in the 20th century, the sultanate came under the influence of the United Kingdom.

When Sultan Sa'id bin Sultan Al-Busaid died in 1856, his sons quarreled over the succession. As a result of this struggle, the empire—through the mediation of the British Government under the Canning Award—was divided in 1861 into two separate principalities: Zanzibar , and Muscat and Oman.

The Hajar Mountains, of which the Jebel Akhdar is a part, separate the country into two distinct regions: the interior, known as Oman, and the coastal area dominated by the capital, Muscat. In 1913, control of the country split. The interior was ruled by Ibadite imams and the coastal areas by the Sultan. Under the terms of the British-brokered Treaty of Seeb of 1920, the Sultan recognised the autonomy of the interior. The Sultan of Muscat would be responsible for the external affairs of Oman.

Muscat and Oman was the object of Franco-British rivalry throughout the 18th century. During the 19th century, Muscat and Oman and the United Kingdom concluded several treaties of friendship and commerce. In 1908 the British entered into an agreement of friendship. Their traditional association was confirmed in 1951 through a new treaty of friendship, commerce, and navigation by which the United Kingdom recognized the Sultanate of Muscat and Oman as a fully independent state.
The Sultan of Oman declared war on Germany on September 10, 1939.

Through focuses it is not hard to grow your industry to a mediocre levels, which can be supplemented by going to limited exports and war economy. Limited Conscription should grant you about 5 12 width divisions. Every few months, you will gain enough manpower to train another division. Like with most small countries, the key ingredient is patience. If possible, put spies in Saudi Arabia and decrypt. By 1939, they usually have about 8 divisions, but they can easily pump out more as needed. You on the other hand, have a small population, so you need to be very careful. In the event Iran gets into a war, you could declare on them, getting a little bit of Iran at the very least. If the UK decolonizes and the Middle Eastern dominions leave the alliance, you will be able to defeat them easily. Yemen should not be hard as long as you decrypt and have air superiority. Depending on how the world situation pans out, you have the option of joining the Allies, Axis, or Comintern. Being non-aligned makes it very easy to go an alternate path. The generic tree should be able to get you far if you play your few cards right. Just like Ethiopia, the challenge is not insurmountable.
Note: If you have the No Step Back DLC and are communist, you can enable Ideological loyalty for your spirit of the Army and get a free weekly +500 manpower boost.
Starting as an 'puppet' state

In the usual case scenario, Oman starts as an colony of the British Empire. In a regular run, chances to become independent are tiring. Having to go through Colony to Dominion and then Freedom, can be irritating. And to achieve the quicker independence, is to select either fascist or communist ideologies. For manpower issue, communism can be the alternative. Boost it by selecting an ideological advisor until it reaches a considerate amount of support.

Opening the political discourse then using the available options, rushing on the ideological branch, along with the ideological advisor, must boost it within a year or so. If the British decolonize, then go with the peaceful transition of power, by going with a held referendum. Otherwise, go with the civil war option, as long as the political support has a decent amount. However, the state of Musandam can be a 50/50 chance. If it falls to your favor, in the civil war, then the road to victory becomes easier. If not, then this delays the civil war a bit longer thus forcing you to research submarines and transport ships in order to naval invade it. Fortunately, you can reload it so this can be fixed. But in Ironman mode, it can be irritating.

Should Oman have any remaining political power, it can be optional to pick the compassionate gentleman advisor in order to core the colony state of 'Imamate of Oman'. Considering that the province does drain the manpower for garrisons. Depending if the British decolonize or not, Oman's priority is to start off independent and sooner or later work on its expansion to unite all of Arab states, from the independent nations to the land owned by the British, French, Italians and Spanish.

Starting in 1936 you have to improve your Manpower and your industries via focus tree. You Need six 8 width divisions in order to win against Saudi Arabia. The default template it's fine, you Just Need to add some support Company as artillery, engineers, recon and field hospital. Declare war as soon as possible and form a defensive line in front of Muscat, you're going to stand there until the "all adults serve" conscription law give you enough Manpower, then you're going to encircle the invaders in south Iman. Next step Is to encircle them in the rub al Kali desert and take the supply hub in Dammam. Be aware of the fact that you can always retire everything to the Muscat defensive line and re-do It all again and again until the enemy runs out of Manpower. You can succeed only micro-managing It all. if u build up forts it's gonna be easier. The key of success Is to save your Manpower killing their troops, Land doesn't matter in this war, except for Muscat. so you're going to defend and encircle them, until they Just can't fight anymore.

The only way to succeed efficiently it's to let them invade you without let them take your supply hubs. When they're overextended Just rush to Sana'a, they're going to capitulate as soon as you take the Capital. In order to do It, you Need the same six 8 width divisions of before. As you have taken both Saudi Arabia and Yemen at this point, Oman can finally take the Arabia formable, increasing the manpower, cores and factories.

Build up 2 divisions more and prepare to invade. Concentrate your troops in the "Al-qassim" area and rush to Najaf and Basra. When you secure these supply hubs Just go North prioritizing supply hubs, until they capitulate. If you do it this way, they're gonna invade the Jawf area, Just to find themself trapped in the desert. With half an army there, you're going succeed in quickly marching on their cities.

GB is always going to try to take Iraq at some point, so you have to anticipate them. Justify war for Socotra, so they won't cover up the rest. You've to take all the Arabian territories fast, except for Socotra. The same 8 divisions of before are going to fit again. At this point start to produce submarines to guard your coast raiding convoy and add an anti-air support to your divisions.
If Axis is doing well, you can build up some divisions and try to take territories around. It is suggested to take Sri Lanka first because it's gonna give you 200k Manpower or so.

If Axis has been lame, you should wait until they're almost done, Just to declare war on them and try to take the Levant area. Your main objective Is to build up a fortified defensive line on Suez, just to economize troops defending against allies when they'll take back Egypt.

The Dragon Rises fascist route

Now, the first thing you should do is take the first Political focus, which will give you 120 political power, plus the 70 you have already accumulated. Use this to get a fascist advisor. Yes, I know, going fascist is the go-to strategy for basically every minor, but if it works, it works. While you wait for fascist support to tick up, take some industrial focuses to get some free factories. Grab the two free civilian factories first, then get the three military factories. By this time you should be above fifty percent fascist support, so hold a referendum to become Ymerodraeth Patagonia. Use your excess political power to get war economy, and if you have any extra left, get some Improved Worker Conditions or Anti-Communist/Democratic raids. This will improve your stability.

At this point, you should've flipped fascist already, so start joining the Axis while Germany deals with the European theatre. At the same time start working on the political focuses. Make a template of paratrooper units, and spam it out. If your units are lacking weapons and the factories cant produce enough in time, use the international markets to make weapon purchases. You should also have a fair amount of political power at this point, so take some stability-increasing decisions and maybe a Captain of Industry. At the same time make an amount of research on planes, notably fighters, medium bombers, and produce at least 50 transport planes. Take the paratrooper units along with the airforce and place them in Western France, if Germany has capitulated France. Establish dropping points into UK, and join once the airforce is ready and trained. It will be time delaying once as you join the war aerial dominance has to be on your favour in order to make landings in Wales, Northern England and London. Germany in this case or any of the Axis powers will automatically provide support for the invasion. Once your paratroopers land in Wales, be sure to rush down and occupy almost all of it before the British troops defeat you in Cardiff.
The Dragon Rises by Brazilian assistance

Another way is to start off the conquest is Brazil, and you have had to annex the allies and control Great Britain especially, if you have earned the "Bad Ending" achievement. Initially, you will build up your Welsh Argentinian cores, notably military factories and dockyards. It should be easy enough, as at this point Welsh Argentina are already your core states. After that, release Wales as an independent nation. And to take some safety measures you can also delete some of the factories on Welsh cores in order to have less resistance in the process. Release Welsh Argentina, switch to play as them and uncheck "release as puppet" not to start off in the wrong foot. Welsh Argentina will possess a few technologies that you as Brazil has researched in the rest of the in game time. Build cheap submarines, only a few suffice to make amends onto naval invasion. Get military and naval access from countries near Wales, even with the political ideology path around them if the neighbouring country is fascist then go fascist. Otherwise if communist, then go communist. Otherwise, if this was done after conquering the world as Brazil, go with the ideology that Brazil has as they will release countries all over the world. As mentioned with Wales neighbours, if Brazil is communist and has a faction, join them if you flipped to communist. The same idea goes if Brazil is fascist instead, then turn fascist as well. Justify on Wales and prepare the navy for its naval invasion. And, subsequently declare war on them. Depending on the player's decision, it can either puppet or annex Wales after its capitulation.
The Dragon Rises by British assistance

Great Britain is another way to go start off the conquest too. But, in this particular situation, it cant release Wales manually. However, with the "London Naval Treaty Signatory" spirit it can bully and harass Argentina in order to get a war declaration through naval treaty decision. Depending on the situation, Argentina is prone to the British pressure and accept navy disarmament. But if it refuses, then you can declare war on Argentina and naval invade from Falkland Islands. Utilize the navy, and bring the airforce and a number of troops to commit to the invasion. Argentina will put up little resistance, but will nonetheless capitulate. In the process, release Welsh Argentina and decide the fate of the rest of the Argentinian lands. Alternatively, Argentina gets an invitation to join the LNT. If refused, this gives a war goal to all signatories. And, stick with the naval invasion program mentioned earlier. Otherwise, should the Argentinian navy disarmament occur instead, then there is another alternative. Go for the "A Change in Course" Focus, turn fascist and manually justify on Argentina. And, follow up with the fascist decision and focuses in the country in order to make manual releases easy. In the meantime, build up military, civilian factories and dockyards in the Welsh Argentinian cores while waiting on the fascist decisions to finish.

After that release Wales, and then "Play as" release Argentinian Wales. As released nation, Welsh Argentina will possess a few technologies that you as Great Britain has researched in the rest of the in game time. Again, build cheap submarines, only a few suffice to make amends onto naval invasion, after going with the Naval Effort focus. Then, with decent political power hire a chief of army for an early army experience boost. After that, go for the political effort. Go communist, and ignite a civil war. is an important metric in relation to convoy escort missions. A new detonator detects the shift in the earth's magnetic field when the torpedo passes under the target. An explosion directly under a ship causes much more damage and often breaks the keel of the target, sinking it instantly.
Equipped with an accoustic detector, the torpedo can home in on the biggest source of noise ahead of it - usually the target.

Instead of leaving an easily-detected trail of bubbles, a torpedo with an electrical engine remains practically invisible until it hits. This also means that there is no trail leading back to the launching submarine.
Every member of a ship's crew, from the Captain down to the simple sailor, must be able to help in containing and fighting fires onboard the ship.
By separating the main water lines around the ship, the probability of a hit rendering the ship completely unable to fight fires is much reduced.
With heavy pumps usually dependent on the main engines for power, a single and fairly light hit in the engine room may render the ship unable to stay afloat.
To hit the target, the first step is to straddle it by firing a few guns at a time until the impacts hit on both sides of the target.

Instead of firing over the target and losing track of the impacts behind the enemy ship, shots are deliberately dropped short of the target and the distance between impact and target measured to determine the range.
Adding small color packages to the shells when they are fired colors the impacts around the target and allows multiple ships to engage the same target without being confused by each other's impacts.

Overview of the Colonial state

Italian State of East Africa, despite being an in-game "nation", by Ironman choices it is unplayable, so the player only benefits playing the nation is by using console commands. Although being the only playable nation without any existing cores, makes up for a challenge upon maintaining peace and order on the owed lands of Ethiopia.
2nd Italo Ethiopian War and colony creation

In order to play as early as Africa Orientale Italiana , is to play first as Italy and finish the war with Ethiopia as soon as possible. Without Ethiopia having to go with the focus of government in exile, because that would prevent from AOI being formed in the first place. Thus, it benefits AOI better to start on the frontline compared to the 1939 scenario as it gets gobbled up by British and French forces in the moment when Italy joins the war with Germany. In the early scenario, the player has to rush down in focuses that releases AOI faster, as in crowning the King of Italy as Emperor of Ethiopia. In a matter of technology, AOI also inherits whatever Italy gains from national focuses or by decision, if the player wishes to remain to play as Italy a little longer just to have their technologies passable for the puppet state, AOI gets them altogether. And, by decision Italy can send manpower to suppress resistance and send weapons.

The colony nation can be released either non aligned or fascist Italy. As it is released with the available and inherited perks as possible, the national spirit, the political advisor, the instantly formed agency and the charismatic leader contribute in generating manpower, maintaining order and keeping the colony slightly stable. Fortunately, as stated earlier, the colony nation inherits most of Italy's technology, ranging from Tanks, planes and navy. Thus, opening opportunities to start and produce if needed necessary. However, being a colony state it has many draw backs. It has a decent amount of factories but some go to the colony's overlord, and some are unusable which have to be resorted to raise compliance above 70%. Therefore, independence and high compliance mean to get the great number of factories back up. Or with other means....
Fighting the Allies in Africa

So the quickest way to spawn infantry units is to use Colonial template units as they have a 6 battalion divisions and no support battalions, and place them everywhere they border the British and the French. And focus nothing more but on producing guns, and building factories manually. The war in East Africa will face AOI having to put up with numeral attacks done by the French and British in the Somaliland cores and all around the British African lands that border AOI. Counterattack once their army fatigues, and try to outmanoeuvre them for a quick encirclement as the enemy troops attack in a thin line. Push them away from Somaliland, and try to link up with the Italian forces up north reaching Egypt. And at the same time, push them away from Sudan, ensuring a direct link route with Italy on the lands of Egypt. Don't forget to secure your southern front, as they have a foothold in Kenya down to Tanzania. Keep in mind, active participation and gains against enemy forces will certainly contribute to an independent Italian State of East Africa.
Contribution Score for the Axis

AOI in order to get a faster and worthy won independence has has to follow and contribute to the capitulation of the Allies. If it has taken care of the situation in the Africa Campaign, AOI has the liberty to move their expedition to Europe. Wait long enough, and USA will eventually join the Allies, which it will make it harder for the Axis.

This requires Germany to have capitulated France had has a foothold on the French soil. Produce Transport planes, and train paratroopers, and prepare to drop from Normandy on certain tiles that are undefended, favourable in East Anglia. Otherwise, train marines and maintain naval supremacy on the English Channel, and naval invade the East British coasts. Rush down to occupy every state in the British islands before Britain reinforces their defences and makes the invasion plans futile. If possible, the Germans will come in need to support the invasion once your troops have already landed. Once the Allies have capitulated, seize all of East Africa in your possession.
Participation in War with USSR

After the Allies have been taken care of, Germany will declare war on USSR. This requires to take the entirety of your available troops and set them in the frontline with the USSR. Make additional gains, push further into their lands with outmanoeuvres, until the crucial cities have been taken. If contributed more than enough, AOI will gain independence by the player' decision.

In the early 20th Century, Ireland experienced increasing tensions in a seven centuries long conflict over English and British rule in Ireland.

Since the 1880s, Irish constitutional nationalists had demanded self-government or “Home Rule” within the United Kingdom. Supporters of immediate true independence were then a small minority. In 1912, Britain accepted these demands. But pro-British unionists in the northern state of Ulster formed paramilitary groups to oppose it, and Irish groups responded in kind. The outbreak of WWI in 1914 stalled both the crisis and implementation of Home Rule.

On 24 April 1916, the “Easter Rising” armed rebellion sought an independent Irish Republic. It had little public support at the time, but Britain's heavy-handed and indiscriminate response to it shifted Irish opinion, beginning a cycle of escalating “physical-force republicanism” and UK reprisals against combatants and civilians alike. This fueled the political rise of the republican Sinn Féin party and its military wing the Irish Republican Army.

The year after WWI ended, the 1919 Irish War for Independence began. By June 1921, a de facto Irish Republic existed but so too a bloody stalemate with no end in sight for either side. The British government, facing intense criticism at home and abroad, offered a truce, which the weary Irish gladly accepted. Contentious negotiations resulted in the Anglo-Irish Treaty of 6 December 1921, establishing the Irish Free State as an autonomous dominion of the Commonwealth. Northern Ireland was created from an area which overall voted to remain part of the United Kingdom.

The Treaty, falling short of a republic, divided the Irish and, in June 1922, the Irish Civil War began. Pro-treaty IRA members, now as the National Army, fought their anti-treaty IRA brothers and Sinn Féin. After 10 grievous months, the pro-treaty forces won. But the war left Irish society divided and embittered for generations. It also allowed Northern Ireland to consolidate its holding of otherwise Irish nationalist counties.

In 1932, the anti-treaty Fianna Fáil party became the majority. They were led by Éamon de Valera, who had been head of the 1921 Irish Republic and subsequently a leader of Sinn Féin but had left in 1927 taking a large faction with him. Ireland still reeling from the Great Depression, de Valera stopped remittance to Britain of farm debts from the 1880s. Retaliatory tariffs by both sides left the Irish economy badly hurt but this Anglo-Irish Trade War ended in the return of military ports to the Irish. This later allowed Irish neutrality in WWII but left British shipping vulnerable to German u-boats.
In 1937, a new constitution was passed which dismantled much of the United Kingdom's control and changed the country's name to Éire, or Ireland.
On 1 September 1939, German troops invaded
, precipitating war with the Allies. On 2 September, the Emergency Powers Act 1939 was introduced to grant government control of the economy and other sweeping powers.

However, Ireland remained neutral throughout the war, despite attacks by both sides on their shipping as well as pressure from the US and a British offer to give them Northern Ireland to join the Allies. Nonetheless, following discovery of IRA attempts to coordinate with the Nazis, the Irish secretly coordinated planning with the UK to defend Ireland from Nazi invasion as a matter of common concern. They also tacitly provided information and preferential treatment to the Allies, such as interning downed Axis pilots while setting Allied pilots free.

If you want to join the Allies it's advisable to focus on your naval and air capacity. You'll struggle to build a large ground force with low manpower so you'll mostly be restricted to support roles. 16 divisions should be enough to protect your territory, as once France and Norway have fallen the Germans will try to invade as you're a softer target than the UK. Build up some coastal forts and AA to protect yourself as if they take Dublin you're going to struggle to kick them out again.

Build your navy around subs, destroyers and use heavy cruisers as your capital ships, you won't have the capacity to build battleships or carriers. Your air force should be comprised of fighters and naval bombers to dominate your waters, you won't need close air support until quite late in the war.

Most of your time should be spent on protecting and raiding convoys in the waters on Northern Europe, through air superiority and mobile raiding fleets you can decimate Axis supply to Norway and pave the way for Allied naval invasions into France. Stay away from large Axis fleets, the Royal Navy can handle them while you mop up smaller forces.

Once the time comes for D-Day you can send attachments of troops and CAS to support the Allied push, move wisely and carefully as manpower will still be an issue and you can't afford to throw units into the meat grinder.

The original Confederate States comprised eleven U.S. states that declared secession from the United States in 1861 and effectively launched an armed rebellion against the same, thus precipitating the American Civil War. The seceding states were South Carolina, Mississippi, Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana, Texas, Virginia, Arkansas, Tennessee, and North Carolina. Additionally, there were also five additional states, those being Delaware, Maryland, Kentucky, Missouri and after 1863, West Virginia, that were culturally and economically connected to the Confederacy and sympathetic to their cause, but did not secede and stayed loyal to the Union. The Confederate States established their own government, first headquartered in Montgomery, Alabama, and then in Richmond, Virginia, with a bicameral Congress and a President alongside his Cabinet, and proceeded to build up and army and navy on their own, with which they waged war against the Union in a bid to achieve independence. The American Civil War lasted from 1861 to 1865 and ended with the total victory of the Union, with the Confederacy and all of its institutions being completely dissolved and its constituent states being reintegrated into the United States during the Reconstruction period of 1865-1877. The Confederate economy was left in ruins and the South was utterly ravaged by the war, leaving it impoverished and destitute compared to the North for well over a century after. More than 150 years later, the American Civil War still casts a shadow over American society and politics, with the spirit of rebellion and resistance to a perceived unjust government in the defense of freedom and rights remaining core tenets in the American mindset, particularly within conservative circles.

With the introduction of special projects in
, all air technologies now also generate aerodynamics and avionics breakthrough progress while being researched. Air technologies are particularly intertwined with the
special projects, which act as prerequisites for many later technologies in the tree.

While fighter aircraft underwent many changes through the Great War, and since, the bi-plane design is becoming obsolete. We must begin to translate civilian technological advances into military applications.
An early fighter modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

Light airframes have been revolutionized with the introduction of radial engines, monoplane designs and all metal skin construction. This design is our attempt at creating our first modern fighter plane.
An early fighter modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

The pace of fighter advancements is astounding, and as such, we must continue to incorporate the technology as well as improve upon existing concepts. Our new fighter design must be capable of high speed, high performance at altitude and the best range possible. Additionally, it must be very well armed.
An improved fighter modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

While our previous generations of fighter plane have proven worthy, any advantage gained by a better design should be taken. This aircraft will be the pinnacle platform of piston-engined fighter that will have excellent power, high agility, deadly weaponry and good range.
An advanced fighter modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

Previous increases in speed pale in comparison to the introduction of the first jet fighters. While we have yet to learn how to best construct planes for these engines, regular fighter planes cannot compete.
New swept wing designs and lighter material choices will allow us to extend the range and speed of the revolutionary jet fighters even further.

Our CAS doctrine requires an aircraft capable of precision surface attack. While these aircraft carry a lesser payload compared to our larger Tactical Bombers, they are capable of attacking and destroying small targets of opportunity through strafing and dive bombing.
Carrier Close Air Support I
An early close air support plane modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

Early war experiences have shown that increased speed, armor and maneuverability are necessary for CAS aircraft survivability against enemy fighters and ground fire. This next generation of ground attack aircraft will also utilize larger bombs, cannons and machineguns to inflict greater damage to their targets.
Carrier Close Air Support II
An improved close air support plane modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

The ever increasing capability of target AA and enemy interceptors require further evolution of our CAS aircraft. The new design incorporates increased engine power, airframe improvements for increased diving capability and protection, as well as even greater payloads.
Carrier Close Air Support III
An advanced close air support plane modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

Naval aviation will be vital in the coming decade to confront new developments in naval warfare, such as the increased importance of submarines. Seaplanes with capacity to work as dive bombers and recon vehicles will be of use.
An early naval bomber modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.
New engine technology and aerodynamically refined designs will boost the speed and diving attack capability of naval planes significantly.
An improved naval bomber modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.
All-metal designs and powerful airbrakes allow for more complex naval aeronautics. The planes of the future will demand a larger crew to operate these advanced systems, however.
An advanced naval bomber modified to launch from and land on aircraft carriers.

It is widely believed that the next war will be won entirely by bombing the enemy to extinction. It is imperative that we begin designing our own bomber plane that is capable of carrying heavy payloads at adequate speed.
Medium bombers need to be versatile and fast, capable of fulfilling a range of roles. A twin-engined design, remaining relatively light, can continue to be of use for many years to come.
Heavier designs of tactical bombers can extend range, payload and speed while maintaining the planes' capacity to perform a wide variety of missions.
Taking a page from the advancements in fighter planes, unconventional materials and shapes can make new designs some of the fastest and best performing twin-engine planes ever built.
The advent of jet fighters necessitates bombers that can outrun or at least match their speed. First-generation medium bombers and bomber-fighters equipped with jet engines will fill this role.
Not content with speed, future jet bombers will set altitude and range records, delivering payloads and performing reconnaissance on intercontinental missions.

Our bomber force needs escort protection from enemy fighters all the way to their targets and back. In order to provide this escort, we must design fighter aircraft with bomber range. Out of necessity these aircraft are larger, slower and less agile than light fighters, though they can carry significant armament.

The war has taught us that our heavy fighter design is vulnerable to more nimble fighters, but quite good at the interception of enemy bombers due to heavy armament. This next design will focus on increased attack capability against enemy aircraft and even ground targets. Its speed and range will be improved as well.

Though our heavy fighter force has shown adeptness in various roles, we must consider a new design that will enhance its ability relative to enemy fighters, as well as allow it to continue intercepting increasingly faster and better defended enemy bombers.

Gathering intelligence on enemy troop movements and providing reports of enemy naval deployments has been the original mission for airplanes since their first deployment in the Great War, and is still an important mission.
By developing dedicated planes for aerial surveillance and long-range reconnaissance, we ensure that we gain and maintain an accurate picture of our opponent's intentions and capabilities.

Experiences from the Great War and studies since show that bombing the enemy's military targets and major cities will win the next war. At the very least, we must have a bomber capable of delivering such destruction. It will need to fly high and at good speed, and it must carry a large payload. This will require a large airframe with multiple engines. It will also have some defensive capability.

Bombing has proven effective at reducing the enemy's capacity to wage war. More defensive weaponry and increased speed will allow a new design to avoid destruction, while increasing the payload and range will make it more effective.
To avoid losses to enemy fighters and ground fire, our next design will fly at great altitude. It will be larger to carry both an enormous payload and more fuel, to increase range.
Multiple jet engines allow new designs unprecedented speed while maintaining a large payload and long range. These planes are built for a new era of weapons of mass destruction.

Without their mothership, the fighters are essentially stranded in the air, severely limiting their operational effectiveness. Strengthening the mothership's air wings is the most cost-effective strategy to enhance the survivability of the entire squadron.
With smaller fighters we will be able to carry more of them into battle without sacrificing much firepower, as well as reducing the weight of the Motherships load
Aerial Hangars attached to the mothership allows us to fit even more miniature fighters onto the top of the aircraft, allowing for increased firepower and further reach.

Switzerland has the longest-standing policy of military neutrality in the world, dating back to the Vienna Congress in 1815, where the European coalition powers agreed that Switzerland should be neutral, and the country has remained so ever since.

Despite being landlocked, wedged between three European major powers and located smack-dab right in the middle of a continent ravaged by war, Switzerland stayed neutral and aggressively maintained that neutrality in both world wars, earning it the reputation of being the ultimate neutral country as it was never invaded even once in either war, whether due to successful deterrence, economic concessions and due to bigger things being at stake.

To maintain said neutrality in World War II, however, Switzerland practised a form of gold trade with both the Allies and the Axis which, in the case of the axis, could be interpreted as a form of money laundering as the gold bought by the Swiss was plundered from national banks across Europe and the swiss francs sold to the Axis were used in commerce with other neutral countries. This, in turn, earned Switzerland something of a reputation of cleverly taking advantage of other peoples' wars for personal profit, with Swiss banking being emblematic for Switzerland, along with chocolate, watchmaking, the Alps and neutrality. Switzerland's neutrality was threatened when Germany considered launching an invasion of Switzerland and Liechenstein with it's allies
but this was later abandoned and the country remained safe from war. For all its faults, Switzerland remained a free democratic country throughout the war and was also a rare safe haven for refugees.
An armed neutrality was maintained throughout the Cold War and remains in place to this day by Switzerland not being a member of either NATO or the
欧洲联盟, despite still being surrounded by European major countries and all of the political, economic, diplomatic, geographic and military intrigue that that entails.

Sinkiang is a province located in the far western region of China, inhabited mostly by the Uyghur, a local Turkic Muslim ethnic group. After the Xinhai revolution, control of Sinkiang was seized by the warlord Yang Zengxin. His rule lasted until 1928, when he was assassinated following the victory of the Kuomintang in the Northern Expedition. The province then fell into a series of wars between multiple sides vying to control the province: Uyghur separatists under the East Turkestan Republic, and the warlords Ma Zhongying, who was aligned with the
Ma Clique, and Sheng Shicai, who was supported by White Russian mercenaries and the

. Sheng won control of the province in 1934, ruling Sinkiang for the next decade with heavy support from the Soviets. The Soviet Union maintained a military base in Xinjiang and had several military and economic advisors deployed in the region. Sheng Shicai would even join the Communist Party of the Soviet Union as a registered member. However, with the Sino-Japanese war raging, he would later turn on the Soviet Union and

共产主义中国, executing Mao Zedong's younger brother, Mao Zemin, and reestablishing relations with the Chinese Nationalist government. In 1944, fearing that Sheng Shicai would turn back to the Soviets, Chiang Kai-Shek removed Sheng from Sinkiang by giving him the ceremonial post of Minister of Agriculture and Forests, which moved him far away to the Chinese capital of Chongqing.

When the Chinese Civil War resumed in 1946, the Soviet-backed Second East Turkestan Republic was formed in Sinkiang and attempted to become independent of the Nationalist government, siding with the communists and peacefully integrating into the newly formed People's Republic of China. Sheng Shicai went into exile in Taiwan with the rest of the Kuomintang.

Sinkiang has the unique ability to proclaim Turkestan after conquering the "Stans" that are in the USSR as well as core all of China. This, along with a starting party of communism, makes Sinkiang distinct from other warlords. But with the least population and only one free building slot for another factory in the entirety of Sinkiang, it will be quite an uphill battle.
Independent action; Opposition and Border Conflicts

First finish "Secure Internal Politics" and "Opposition". Prepare 6 divisions that are optimized for high soft attack to win border conflicts quickly; or at least what one may scrounge together before Japan performs Marco Polo. Do not go to war with Japan. Immediately justify war against Xibei San Ma while quickly speeding through the Border Conflict focuses to be able to do border conflicts with the Nationalists. Once the justification is complete, go to war. Upon winning, begin border conflicts with the Nationalists to ensure a direct line to the Yunnan Clique then to Guangxi by extension. Occupy them for resources while also attempting to encircle Nationalist China to prevent the Japanese from potentially capitulating them, as the Japanese should not have military access through you. Be warned: the state where a border conflict happens is somewhat random, and several unlucky happenings may leave the player with just a small share of the China pie in the end, and you'll have to fight longer for the rest.

While seemingly the weakest warlord, Sinkiang has one key advantage of not being non-aligned as with the other warlords. This allows justification of war regardless of world tension and makes it possible to join Comintern at start. Since the USSR has no interest whatsoever to any Chinese territory, you can justify on other warlords and have the USSR win the wars for you, and claim the land for free. One may also beg for the equipment desperately needed, though the Soviet Union tends to have a large equipment deficit, so you may have to resort for guns from elsewhere, such as Germany after the Anchluss.
Starting as Communist also has the advantage of being able to replace Communist China by going through the

instead of the parallel Warlord Communist branch of the focus tree. This way, you are not forced to give the USSR a tribute, nor worry about giving them a war goal on you should you decide to default on it.

With as much of China under the player's control for manpower, resources and industry, it becomes time to took at the Soviet Union if one wishes to maximise cores. By the time one finishes unifying China, if the game is set on Historical focuses, the German Reich may be preparing or are undertaking Operation Barbarossa, in which case the player should be prepared to rush in and gobble up as much of Central Asia as possible. An ideal time to strike may be about two years in or if the Germans approach Moscow or the Caucuses mountains.

Should the game deviate from the historical timepoints, it may be advisable to let the USSR or its successor state slog its way through the Gobi Desert and fight a defensive attritional warfare with copious artillery and anti-air before making a final counterattack with advanced tanks.
