The division designer is a utility located in the "Recruit & Deploy" menu of the user interface. The division designer enables players to create organizational templates for divisions, which are units that can be assigned to command groups and engaged in land warfare. Once created, these templates can then be trained, equipped, and deployed. Modifications to templates are automatically applied to all divisions that utilize that template. In order to transition divisions to a new template on an individual or rolling basis rather than all at once, it is possible to make the template change in a duplicate template and then reassign the divisions to the modified template when desired.

It is important for players to be aware of the potential for enhancing their forces by incorporating superior templates as they accrue experience in the game, given that the initial formations of most countries do not align with optimal standards. The initial units are typically smaller or composed exclusively of infantry, and their effectiveness is enhanced when additional troop types are incorporated.
Editing a template in the division designer.
As every nation starts with some form of basic template, it is often advisable to edit this as technology,
army experience, manpower and equipment become available. It is also possible to design a template from the ground up using the
option in the template selection menu.

With the 1.5 patch, templates can now have a name-list too, with historical unit names selected. This function renames all templates of this type according to the list selected. The names appear in white type in contrast to green division names that are a custom function . The name list itself is not editable except through mods.
This division won't receive M1 Garand rifles.

To the right of the parachute icon is the Division Equipment button. Selecting this button will bring up a new menu showing all of the equipment stockpiled that the template can use. This allows the player to control what specific weapon types the units with this template may use, so it is valuable if the player is seeking to have certain units use older equipment and stockpile a reserve of new equipment for other units or other purposes such as lend-lease shipments. Equipment already in the field won't be returned unless it is replaced by an upgrade or the template changes so that type is no longer used.

Below the division equipment button and to the right of the template name are the division priority options. Divisions with higher priorities will receive equipment and reinforcements before divisions with lower priorities. A template can have one of three priority options:
: Units with this template will receive equipment last and at the lowest priority once deployed. Perfect for units set to guard bases or control resistance.

The right side of the division designer show the stats of the currently selected template. These stats will change as battalions and companies are added or removed from the division.

Below the main stats window is a hardness indicator, shown as a bar with a tank icon to the left and an infantry helmet icon to the right. Some equipment, motorized and tanks in particular, have a hardness stat represented by a percentage. This stat contributes to the overall hardness of the division they are in. Divisions with high hardness take less damage from soft attacks, but receive more damage from hard attacks. To increase a template's hardness, add more units with higher hardness stats, or remove them to increase softness.

Players can select the colonial templates icon to view subjects' templates.

are able to recruit divisions using their subjects' templates. Subject forces draw equipment from their overlord and manpower from both their home country and their overlord. How much manpower comes from each depends on the subject's autonomy level. Colonies must provide for 70% of a division's manpower, puppets must provide 90%, and integrated puppets must provide 100%. Countries cannot recruit from a dominion, although they may still request the dominion to provide forces. Although subject forces are under complete control of their overlord, they can only be deployed in their home country, from which they may travel elsewhere. One cost of deploying them is that increases the subject's autonomy.

In order to recruit subject forces, select the colonial templates button in the upper-right corner of the templates panel. This will bring up a list of available subjects where troops can be raised, as well as show their autonomy level. Select a subject to see a list of their division templates. From here the templates can be viewed or copied. Selecting the copy button will place a copy of that template into the home country's template list, where they can be edited using the overlord's Army Experience. Colonial templates will show the flag of their home country to the bottom-left of their icon.

Each country has a set of preliminary division templates, some of which will already be in use by existing divisions. A significant number of these templates encompass a single type of battalion and lack the inclusion of any support companies. It is possible that they may prove useful in the role of occupation or garrison troops, despite their lack of apparent combat capability. Mobile units are capable of outpacing infantry units and are a valuable asset for an army. Divisions that include cavalry may prove valuable in this role for an extended period.

It is often advantageous to retain a copy of the original form of a template that is being modified, as this allows it to be used as a base for subsequent designs, thereby saving experience points . Furthermore, these templates can be readily replicated and stored under a distinct designation within the Division Designer.

is a releasable nation in Norway, encompassing one state on the Artic coast, which is mountainous and a wasteland. In the 1936 start date, its territory is controlled by

, the nation with the lowest core population of all pre-existing nations.

During World War II, continental Norway was invaded and occupied by Germany in spring 1940. The four-man team on Jan Mayen stayed at their posts and in an act of defiance began sending their weather reports to the United Kingdom instead of Norway. The British codenamed Jan Mayen 'Island X' and attempted to reinforce it with troops to counteract any German attack.

The Germans attempted to land a weather team on the island on 16 November 1940; the German naval trawler carrying the team crashed on the rocks just off Jan Mayen after a patrolling British destroyer had picked them up on radar. The detection was not by chance, as the German plan had been compromised from the beginning with British wireless interceptors of the Radio Security Service following the communications of the Abwehr concerning the operation, and the destroyer had been waiting. Most of the crew struggled ashore and were taken prisoner by a landing party from the destroyer.

The Allies returned to the island on 10 March 1941, when the Norwegian ship Veslekari, escorted by the patrol boat Honningsvaag, dropped 12 Norwegian weathermen on the island. The team's radio transmissions soon betrayed its presence to the Axis, and German planes from Norway began to bomb and strafe Jan Mayen whenever weather permitted, but did little damage. Soon supplies and reinforcements arrived, and even some anti-aircraft guns, giving the island a garrison of a few dozen weathermen and soldiers. By 1941, Germany had given up hope of evicting the Allies from the island and the constant air raids stopped.

Panama, arguably the weakest nation in the Americas, gets the decision to form

If one wishes to achieve greatness as the small, split in two nation of Panama, taking this decision will tremendously help and skyrocket her core population, from less than half a million to more than twenty million, turning it into the second most populated country in Latin America and putting it on par with nations like
. But how would one be supposed to take Panama there? Their starting manpower is laughable and only slightly higher than
's manpower. It goes without saying that one will need some help in forming

大哥伦比亚. It should also be noted that to make things easier, one should play on Historical AI Focuses mode so as to prevent the United States from enacting their Pax Americana in early 1937, thus blocking Panama from any attempts at expansion.

First of all, one should take Political Effort as their starting focus, and get the Fascist Politician as soon as possible: the clock is already ticking. One's next two purchases should be Free Trade and Limited Conscription, and then one should start saving up their political power. Also, one should build a port in the southernmost province of the left side of the country, and not trade for any resources just yet: Panama's lone civilian factory is desperately needed. One will need to research submarines and naval invasions, as well as planes and paratroopers. Getting better guns and artillery is also a good idea. Once the first focus is done, one should go for Naval Effort and start producing some convoys until the port construction is done, then start producing some submarines; it is worth noting that one single submarine should provide enough naval capacity for the following years, so switching back to convoy production early can be a good idea. One can then make their way into the Industrial foci. The order one takes them in does not really matter. One should have their first submarine ready by early-mid 1937.

Once Panama's politics switch to fascism, it should ready itself for the many wars she will face in the foreseeable future. One may start going down the Fascist route in the focus tree for the extra 7%
. By this point one should have two divisions of the default template. One should then justify a war goal on

should be Panama's main division providers, as they have the two highest populated states in Central America, and El Salvador will likely have already taken the +7% recruitable population from its focus tree.

, all naval technologies now also generate naval engineering breakthrough progress while being researched.
To ensure the safety of convoys, the destroyers of the Great War must be repurposed and developed. Arming vessels with more torpedoes will allow more opportunities to engage.
Longer torpedo range and faster reload speeds, along with new types of armaments such as anti-air turrets, will allow our destroyers to remain efficient and versatile.
To better face threats from above and below, new destroyers must be outfitted with radar and modern anti-air and anti-submarine weaponry.
The modern destroyer must be fitted with a variety of different detection technologies, new depth charge deployment systems and be built at a larger scale than their predecessors.

Although bound by the stipulations of the Washington Naval Treaty, the cruiser is still the most flexible warship. This hull allows construction of a light cruiser for screening and scouting, or a heavy cruiser to support the battleline.
The next generation of cruisers features new engine arrangements that improve survivability, as well as space for dedicated aircraft facilities.
As cruisers around the world get more powerful and capable, new and larger hulls are needed to hold all the extra equipment needed.

Influenced by wartime experiences, the latest generation of cruisers have a rearranged superstructure to allow wider fields of fire for anti-air armaments and new internal layouts to support the use of radar.
An improved pneumatic mechanism allows much larger airplanes to be launched via catapult. This increases their search radius.

Considered by some to be a relic of a bygone era of naval warfare, by others as the most impressive ships ever built, no one can deny that these remnants of the battleship arms race constitute some of the most heavily armed and armored vessels ever built.
With improved stability and range, a new generation of battleships improve upon previous designs while remaining within limits stipulated by naval treaties.

Thicker armor, stronger engines, a battery of high-caliber guns and improved anti-air capabilities can allow battleships to remain relevant, if correctly employed, in a world where naval warfare is increasingly dominated by aerial support.
As the world sees what may be the last major battleship confrontations, the importance of heavy armaments and anti-air turrets is greater than ever.

Conversions of old hulls allow for cheap experiments with naval aviation to gain experience in building and operating carriers. These ships will be less capable than a purpose-built carrier, but far quicker to create.
Many military theorists believe that naval aviation is the future. Converting old capital ships and ocean liners to carry aircraft will be the first step towards utilizing these new doctrines.
As work begins on the first keel-up carrier designs, we must ensure that these ships have the range and speed to keep up with the rest of our navy, while respecting the post-war naval treaties.
Improved construction methods and more specialized systems like deck edge elevators allow these carriers to transport more planes more efficiently.

The role of the submarine in the fleet outside of convoy attacks is still under debate. Achieving a balance between combination of speed, range and weaponry will be key to the necessary model.
Increased test depth and efficient layouts will be features of the modern submarines, taking advantage of field experience to select appropriate armaments and engines.
A simple airtube running from the engine room to the control tower. Extended, it allows the submarine to run its engines and charge its batteries while still submerged.

Even though Paraguay is a landlocked nation with almost no industry, manpower or resources, Paraguay has a neighbor called

that is in a very similar position. However because Paraguay is a communist country it can justify wars right from the beginning in 1936. What this strategy consists of is to justify a war as soon as you can against Bolivia. Once you have your war goal ready, you will stay in a defensive position on the border with Bolivia because the Bolivian AI will endlessly attack your line. After a period of time the Bolivians will have lost most of its manpower and equipment attacking your line and they won't be able to break through. When you see that the Bolivians are low on equipment then you can start to push and invade their lands without too many problems. Again though the key is to be entrenched and let their army grind away on your front line until their troops are weakened. Once this happens only then should you put your army on the offensive. It may be worthwhile to consider building land forts and infrastructure on the border before the war to make things easier on your army when the Bolivian AI starts to grind away on you. Then when you capitulate them, you will just annex them. After this you can attack other countries . Be warned though no matter which other neighbour you attack next, it will be more difficult. Chile has among the strongest infantry division templates in South America at the very start of the game, and being only a few tiles wide you may have to deal a long war as you take the country one tile at a time as you make your down to the capital. In essence Chile will do the same thing to you as what you want to do with the Bolivians. Alternatively you could try to attack Peru or Argentina however both have larger armies and more manpower meaning in order to win you need finish the war as quickly as possible before they can produce more divisions. It is probably worth producing paratroopers for these options as you can land forces behind their lines to either pull forces off their front or conversely to pin down forces so they can't reinforce divisions your frontline army can defeat. It is strongly advisable to not attempt to attack Brazil unless you have conquered at least two other neighbouring nations to gain more manpower and factories. Another option is to join the Second World War by joining one of the factions, however if you do this while tensions are high and you are attempting to conquer one of your neighbours it will likely result in the other nation joining an opposing faction. The most obvious faction to join would be the Soviet Union in the Comintern as you already are communist and can join at any point. Or the Axis if you go fascist though this means one would have to switch ideologies. Even though you can join in on the side of the Allies, this would probably result in much less territorial expansion.

A Border War is a small scale conflict. A way to acquire a State without going through the dangers of full scale warfare. It is primarily focused on China and its communist/nationalist conflict, but other nations can also get decisions to enact border incidents against other countries. And for Communist China, in particular, it is
early-game gameplan. As it is largely decision and event driven, the rules can be a bit confusing.

It goes through a number of phases: The decision to cause a border incident, the decision to commit to combat, the combat, the optional decisions to escalate the conflict, and the result. It is limited to two parties: Aggressor and Defender .

A border conflict starts with the appearance of a decision to create a border incident. It requires finding the right parties to conflict over. If multiple countries are eligible targets, there will be one decision for each of them.
This decision is visible if:
No other Border Conflict has been initiated between the two parties
Neither party is in the same Faction or a subject of the other
The Decider has the Flag CHI_institute_cross_border_raids and neither Aggressor nor Defender are the Leader of China. (Comment: Warlord goes opposition can border war all other warlords
The Decider has the Flag CHI_provoke_border_clashes and the target is the Leader of China
The Target has the Flag CHI_provoke_border_clashes and the decider is the Leader of China
The Decider has the Flag CHI_anti_opposition_campaigns and both sides picked focuses to support in the Nationalist/Communist Conflict
The Decider is Communist China and the target cooperates with the Nationalists
The Target is any of the Chinese Factions
The Decider is any of the Chinese Factions
and having a direct border with
and has completed the focus Seize the Panamá Canal
and has completed Intervention focuses
and has completed the focus Stage an Incident in the Bosporus
This decision is available if the aggressor:
fully owns and controls a source state
has at least 1 division in the source state
does not have a active Border Conflict anywhere else
does not have a NAP with the Defender

The Decision costs 100 PP and runs for 30 days. Upon taking the decision, a random Defender State without an active border conflict is chosen. Then a random neighboring attacker State is also chosen. The decision can not be taken again for 180 days . The defender is informed and both the defender and aggressor have the 30 days to bring troops in the states into position.

After the initial warning timeout has run its course, the attacker has 30 days to decide to actually commit to the conflict. If they do, combat starts instantly. This can be used to prepare more forces. Or to reconsider, if the defenders forces or global situation no longer supports a conflict. However if the timer runs out, the Aggressor loses another 100 PP.
After the incident has been created and the conflict committed to, a combat will start:
6 Divisions from both states are picked and moved into a separate army. This army is given a random Leader from the countries pool. These two Armies then enter combat.
Aside from moving divisions out of the State, there seems to be no way to control which divisions are picked and the selection seems to be entirely random. This is outside of mod-able code.
Equally the leader is randomly picked from across the country pool. This can include any Generals or Field Marshals currently in action or duty at another front. No leader ability can be used.
The armies are locked and neither side can add or remove divisions, put them under a field marshal or otherwise affect them until the conflict is over.
The combat has a width of respective terrain and all units start in reserve. Which can result in one or both sides having 0 divisions actively fighting, dealing no damage to each other.
Selected Divisions that are not at the border first have to move there, before they are placed in reserve and can then join. This mostly applies to selected divisions that were on garrison duty.
If not enough divisions are in the State, additional units will be drawn from across the country. These units still have to first move there.
AI Divisions that dropped out due to Organization loss will move away to recover to full, then rejoin the fight as reserve. Player divisions that drop out will not return to the fight.
Planning bonus and commander abilities remain in effect.
If nobody wins the conflict within 360 days, the conflict is declared a draw
Both sides can decide to escalate the conflict. There is a 45 day cool-down between those options
costs 200 PP, increases the width to 100 and gives both sides a +15% bonus.
turns this into a full blown war after 15 days, canceling the border conflict and the combat.
Both sides can also decide to
of the conflict, causing a instant win for the other side.
If the attacker wins, they gain 100 PP and control of the State. On the last state, the target is instead annexed.
If the defender wins, they gain 150 PP, 30 Army XP, and a Tech bonus of 100% to 1 land doctrine. The attacker loses 150 PP instead.
If the conflict is canceled both sides gain 30 Army XP and 50 PP.

The attacker will NOT be able to start another border war against the same defender if he fails to initiate the conflict. Cool down period is 180 days for same defender, regardless of victory or defeat.
It is always 6 divisions that are picked, regardless of width. Accordingly, it can help to design, and encourage the picking of, high-width divisions.

When fighting a border war it’s important to have as many modifiers which increase attack as possible. Since your divisions' location within the state doesn’t matter, and terrain modifiers aren’t in effect either, make sure your troops are placed where they get sufficient supply, so you won’t get a debuff from low supply.
The experience gain to manpower loss ratio for Border wars is exceptionally good, leading to a handful of extremely skilled divisions which can be used for later operations.
Terrain, entrenchment, and other defensive modifiers are NOT ignored. There is a considerable advantage for the defender due to Defense tending to be higher then Breakthrough.
The defender can win by outlasting the enemy for the entire 360 days.
The attacker has to win by actually crushing the enemy with enough damage. But failing that, a draw is preferable over a defeat.
While leader abilities cannot be used during the conflict, they can be chosen just before it and still should have effect.
As all units start in reserve, the reinforcement rate is extremely important

The AI is unable to manipulate the divisions chosen for the combat and bring units into play. Often their garrison Cavalry Divisions are drawn into the combat. However it just having a manned frontline against the player will drastically improve the expected enemy troop quality.
Your troops' logistic priority will start unmotorized regardless of its previous setting.
The selection of which units join the fight can not be affected in any known way.
The decisions and results however are script driven and thus fully mod-able.
It is worth noting that the strait crossing penalties do still apply, as they were likely not considered for mainland china.

Following the Second Boer War , South Africa was incorporated into the British Empire, becoming a self-governing dominion in 1910 as the Union of South Africa. Governed by a white minority, the Union implemented policies that entrenched racial segregation, such as the 1913 Natives Land Act, which restricted land ownership for Black South Africans. In 1931, the Statute of Westminster granted South Africa full legislative independence, enabling it to make its own decisions within the framework of the British Commonwealth. However, tensions persisted between pro-British factions and Afrikaner nationalists, many of whom sought greater autonomy from Britain.

Between 1936 and 1939, political and social divisions in South Africa intensified. The Representation of Natives Act removed Black South Africans from the Cape voters’ roll, further entrenching their political disenfranchisement. During this period, Afrikaner nationalist organizations such as the Ossewabrandwag gained prominence, expressing sympathy for Nazi ideology and reflecting anti-British sentiment among some Afrikaners.

Prime Minister J.B.M. Hertzog, an Afrikaner nationalist, advocated for South African neutrality as tensions in Europe escalated toward World War II. His stance clashed with that of Jan Smuts, a pro-British leader who supported South Africa’s alignment with the Allies. In 1939, Hertzog’s neutrality policy was defeated in Parliament, leading to his resignation. Smuts succeeded him as Prime Minister and brought South Africa into the war on the side of the Allies, despite opposition from nationalist factions.

Construction of fortifications and breaching obstacles make combat engineers vital in the field. Giving our engineers a versatile role enables us to deploy them in the diverse situations where they will be needed.
Combining engineering expertise with armored protection, armored engineer units are specialized on clearing obstacles and supporting front-line advances under heavy fire.
With modern equipment and high explosives, our engineers can go beyond their traditional tasks and surprise the enemy with their ingenuity, at land and sea.
Military engineering projects are approaching a larger scale. The construction of advanced infrastructural aid enables operations requiring supplies beyond what is normally available in the field.

Maintaining local mobility while constructing what would previously have been considered permanent fortifications and supply systems, combat engineers of the future will ensure that no matter where our troops are attacked, they will be prepared.
Sending smaller groups to scout ahead before moving in the main force allows us to gather intelligence about where the enemy is and how many we are facing.
Helicopters are able get a good vantage point of the battlefield regardless of the actual terrain, and thus make excellent forward scouts to provide accurate feedback to artillery barrages.

Reconnaissance missions are often dangerous and casualties are high. Preparing our patrols to move and withdraw rapidly and equipping them to clear obstacles placed by the enemy will increase their chances of coming back alive.
Improvements in radio technology change the way reconnaissance missions can be executed, enabling rapid communication of the gathered intelligence.
Deep reconnaissance operations, mixing espionage, guerilla operations and commando training, will aid our tactical choices and allow us to adapt our decision-making rapidly.

Regular troops may be able to manage occupation for a shorter period of time, but they are first and foremost soldiers. Integrating military police into our forces will ensure we have people on the ground to respond to resistance and investigate sabotage.

Equipped with military motorbikes, these units are tasked with maintaining order behind the lines, escorting convoys, and conducting patrols. Their speed and mobility allow them to quickly respond to disruptions and, if needed, perform reconnaissance in active combat zones.

By engaging in regular police duties in occupied territories, such as traffic control and maintaining public order, our military police can minimize the chaos and confusion in which partisan movements can thrive in.
Cooperating with local spy networks and informers established before occupation, our military police can proactively prepare for where resistance is likely to arise.

Safely policing occupied territory is as much about returning to normalcy as it is about ruthlessly eliminating opposition. Our military police must ensure that this process starts early, to ensure safety for soldiers and civilians alike.
Maintenance, repair and overhaul are important to keep military equipment reliable and safe to use. Having companies dedicated to this will ensure that it's given appropriate attention.
The use of armored recovery vehicles enables our maintenance personnel to recover and repair all kinds of equipment, ensuring maximum operational readiness on the battlefield.
Routine operational maintenance procedures minimize the risks of equipment breaking down and alerts troops to replace it before it does.
Making sure that our troops always have the basic materials in the field to perform common repairs will prevent the continued use of equipment known to be damaged.
Experiences with designing for active redundancy in the Great War can be renewed to work with more modern equipment to make maintenance easier.
A casualty doesn't need to mean a dead soldier. Having immediate medical attention available for our wounded brought back to the rear is the first step towards ensuring this.
Incoming wounded! We have incoming wounded! Helicopters provide even faster casualty evacuation than regular ambulances.
By establishing the use of portable hospitals, bringing the medical care to where it is needed, we can stop many unnecessary deaths and permanent injuries.

Surgery is among the most common emergency procedures needed in the field. Procedures and tools for this must be available closer to the front, and we must ensure that skilled surgeons are part of the military medical units.

Although many improvements have been made in field medicine, many advances are improvised and we lack an established doctrine. With more experience, we can explain the role of these units more clearly and make improvised innovations permanent fixtures.
Having specialized Logistics Officers among our ranks will ensure that support networks are leveraged to minimize waste.

Helicopters equipped with transport pods or towing goods beneath them on a line can move supplies and equipment quickly and without regard for terrain. Getting stuck in the mud is a thing of the past!
Adapting our risk analyses to the new circumstances of war will improve the safety of our logistical support.
Continued statistical evaluation of troop supply needs contribute to maximizing the utility of our resources.
Developing standardized classifications for supplies will minimize confusion and make planning more efficient.

Establishing and maintaining communications in the field has always required special skills. With the advent of new communications and detection technology in the Great War, new possibilities for the practice lie ahead.
Equipping our units with command vehicles will ensure secure and reliable battlefield communications and coordination under armored protection.

Signal companies focusing on communication between the different branches of the military can ensure that ground forces are able to coordinate efforts with sea and air operations and plan their movements more rapidly.
Increasingly portable communications technology is more viable to be personally carried as a backpack. This increased mobility of signal corps must be utilized.

Among our signal specialists are people with unparalleled first-hand knowledge of field use of this equipment. By involving them in the research of new communication technologies, we can make use of their expertise.

Taken over by the military from regular civilian freight duty, this train engine is well-suited to move a large amount of supplies over long distances. However, its civilian construction makes it vulnerable.
A train engine encased in heavy armor to make it less vulnerable to enemy attack. It can carry as much cargo as any other design, but is more expensive to produce.
A heavy cannon mounted on a railway carriage for transportation.

A simplified design that ommits many features commonly found on regular freight trains for the sake of cheaper production. It is still every bit as vulnerable as a regular train, but can more easily be replaced.

In a starting scenario Ecuador is not a very powerful country. Being surrounded by powerful neighbors, especially at a brink of war with Peru, it risks losing its provinces or getting annexed. With a small population and a small underequipped force, a tiny air force of 12 P-6 planes and a democratic government it is unlikely to unlock its potential for expansion. In this case, becoming Gran Colombia.

Politically wise, it would be preferable to become Fascist, or becoming Communist. As it will serve to justify goals much quicker on your northern neighbor Colombia along with Panama and Venezuela. Additionally with their perks, it will solve up manpower issues if given time. And, make sure to rush down for industrial focus, as having more factories, civilian or military, will certainly help. The best option to improve your army performance against Peru is to build land forts and just in case coastal forts . And train as much infantry to set them in the Peruvian border, and leave a small defensive infantry brigade of 4 battalions to defend the capital, and the Galapagos island. As time passes by and the tensions rise, consider upgrading the army with few support battalions, and research Marine troops. Because of the Jungle terrain that both countries share, it will be beneficial for Ecuador to gain the upper hand. Request license for the P-6 planes from the US, or from another country for a fighter plane depending on the players choice, as researching one will take time as well. For extra air defense, research and build anti aircraft to prevent the enemy aircraft gain superiority on your airspace. Be sure to built railways to connect supply hub to the frontline.

At a certain point, while preparing the defenses, Peru will declare war on you without warning. Both nations gain the Amazonian War buff, that unfortunately, cannot join a faction, but gain infantry buffs, and a 2% recruitable population. Fortunately, in Ecuador's case, it will gain additional 5 infantry brigades that spawn in the border with Peru which will help to turn the tide. You will stay in a defensive position on the border with Peru because the Peruvian AI will endlessly attack your line. After a period of time the Peruvians will have lost most of its manpower and equipment attacking your line and they won't be able to break through. When you see that the Peruvians are low on equipment then you can start to push and invade their lands without too many problems. Again though the key is to be entrenched and let their army grind away on your front line until their troops are weakened. Once this happens only then should you put your army on the offensive. It may be worthwhile to consider building more land forts and infrastructure on the border before the war to make things easier on your army when the Peruvian AI starts to grind away on you. Then when you capitulate them, you will just annex them.

After the war is finished in your favor, the road for expansion has been opened. What remains to be done is to take the war at their land, one nation at a time. And, hopefully neither of them has joined a bigger faction or a domestic faction such as the Mexican led Bolivarian alliance
Conquest of Colombia and Panama

Colombia is the next nation for the challenge. Although similarly stronger as Peru, it possesses more strength than the latter, albeit and a bigger navy. But less of a chance for naval invasion. And, the sole option remains on continuing the land warfare with them. Their terrain is a mix of Jungles and Mountains, thus it is advised to deploy Mountaineer troops, not to forget to adjust support battalions on their way. Last but not least, be sure to have taken special forces doctrines for Marines and Mountaineers to increase your favors in your odds. Same starting strategy to be applied just like with the Peruvian War beforehand. Push the troops on the offensive line after they have been worn out from their attack. In the meantime, if Colombia is halfway done for capitulation, be sure to justify on Panama. It paints as an easy target, and fortunately the capital city is close to the Colombian border, making it quick to capitulate. Be quick to seize them first, as it will fall randomly in the hands of the Mexican forces if they go for the Central American focus

Venezuela has a larger army and will put up more of a fight. It is likely to join a faction, or has already joined one, if the tensions are high and more troops will fill the frontlines. Be sure to justify on them quickly, and bring more of the inherited arsenal on force display against them. The Colombian prized navy, air force, the special forces and by this point have researched tanks. The scenario is similar with Colombia in terms of terrain, and it is the right time to utilize naval invasions, as your army in the frontline pin down the bordering troops. Annex them immediately, and sooner or later, you will form Gran Colombia

Gaining its independence in 1830 from

, Uruguay was, throught most of its history, plagued with political instability, thanks to the meddling of foreign nations. This led to a civil war in 1836 between the Colorado and Nacional parties, both of which gained major military backing from foreign powers and led to a Colorado victory.

This pattern continued, with Colorado and Blancos waging war against each other throught most of the 19th century, up until 1904, where the last major civil war occurred that resulted in a Colorado victory, which began an era where the Colorado party gained an hegemony over the political landscape of Uruguay.

To avoid another civil war from ever happening again, Uruguayan politicians created a new constitution, which divided the executive power between the president and the newly created Consejo Nacional de Administración. This council was made out 9 members, 2/3 of which would correspond to the winning party in the elections and the other third would be made out of the losing party. This guaranteed some power to the losing party and allowed some power to be shared.

This reform proved effective and Uruguay entered an era of peace, however, critics of the system pointed out the slow responses to the Great Depression. One of the biggest critics of the system, President Gabriel Terra of the Colorado party, with support of the Blancos, the police and the military, moved in to dissolve the council. This began a period known as "Terra's Dictatorship", where Gabriel Terra began censoring the press, restricting civil liberties and cracking down on dissent, leading to the exile and arrest of many important political figures. To protest this move, various politicians of the Colorado party, including former president Baltasar Brum, urged the people to rebel. However, after no major resistence to the coup occurred, and being denied the option of exile by Terra, Baltasar Brum walked to the middle of a busy street, and shot himself on the heart, screaming "¡Viva Batlle! ¡Viva la libertad!".

What followed were years of political tension, with various attempts to dislodge the Terra regime from office, like the 1935 revolution, but none succeeded. Eventually, Terra began a reform to the constitution, which disolved the Council, allowed women suffrage and scheduled elections in 1938.

In 1939, the German battle cruiser Admiral Graf Spee docked in Montevideo harbor after being chased by British ships in the Atlantic. However, the Urugayan authorities refused to let the ship stay in their waters. The ship left the harbor and sunk itself in Montevideo bay to avoid capture.

Strategy for the Maphilindia conquest

As the Philippines, rush down the monarchist path as fast as possible up to the war for independence. If you're lucky, America will just give you independence without having to do the war - otherwise reset since its relatively early. After independence, just keep allying and attempting to annex as many Hispanic nations as possible, ideally the ones with the most manpower or factories first . These annexations can actually be savescummed even in ironman mode, but the most critical one is Spain - if they reject annexation/allying, you need to reset or savescum. From here, strategy is dependent on circumstances & preference. If playing on historical mode, you should attempt to Sealion the UK with the Axis - you can join the faction for their assistance flooding troops in after landing/paradropping, but defeating the UK is significantly harder in historical now as a minor nation without tanks or air . If you can't kill the UK in historical before the US joins the allies or a dominion becomes a major, you have to defeat them as well. Even if you can kill the UK, you need to have gained enough warscore to annex both the Indian and Malaysian & Indonesian states required for the achievement . As of 1.19.1 not all Indonesian states are required for the "Form Maphilindo" decision, so keep that in mind for the peace deal. Do the "Malayo-Polynesia" focus to get claims on Malaysia and Indonesia and therefore will be cheaper in the peace deal. Also note that the achievement description is misleading, you need specifically the Indian states from the achievement requirements.

Alternatively, an ideal ahistorical mode can lead to an early independent India, which you can simply invade and annex . After this, you just need to occupy certain Indonesian/Malaysian states to be able to click the decision, which is a lot easier since it doesn't require a peace deal. Another ahistorical setup that may be easier to manipulate is just one without America in the Allies, which can arise from the communist/democratic/nonaligned Japanese paths. In this scenario, you just need to get strong enough to beat the UK, which allows for more buildup time. Alternatively to all of the above, you can just invade America early after annexing/allying Mexico, which would give you all the resources you need to beat Britain. However, it's hard to get a wargoal on them without them joining the allies anyway, and it's a major detour if you want to actually get the achievement in a reasonable amount of time.

The Unaligned States of America is a peculiar state, having a rather obscure historical basis even by HOI4 standards. While the

incarnation of the original Confederate States from the first American civil war, established in opposition of the growing communist movement in the United States, the Unaligned States of America has a much more obscure historical background.

The election of Franklin Delano Roosevelt as President of the United States in 1932 alarmed many conservative businessmen, bankers and industrialists at the time, who believed that his New Deal program would lead to both reckless public spending, government overreach and also create fertile ground for socialist and communist movements to proliferate and grow out of control. These businessmen viewed any currency not backed by the Gold Standard as inflationary and harmful to both private and public finances as well as putting America on the path to nationwide bankruptcy.

In response to this, between 1932 and 1934, a secret political conspiracy was developed, known today as the "Business Plot" or "Wall Street Putsch". In this plot, the conservative business establishment would engineer a coup d'état against Roosevelt's government, under the pretext that the president's health was failing . To facilitate this, the plotters would create a fascist veteran's organization and assemble and army of 500 000 men, with the former Bonus Army members at its core, to march on Washington D.C. To lead this army, the plotters attempted to recruit major general Smedley Butler, who had previously partaken in the Spanish-American War and the Banana Wars between 1898 and 1934 and encouraged the Bonus Army demonstration in 1932, which led to Roosevelt's election. Butler's good reputation and popularity was perceived to be vital for the success of the coup, and he was seen as "easier to manipulate" than other military leaders. Given a successful coup, Smedley Butler would have been installed into power in the newly created position of "Secretary of General Affairs", where he would wield near-absolute power while Roosevelt would have assumed a figurehead role. This would effectively have established him as a fascist, corporatist dictator and greatly expanded the power of Big Business in the United States. The plot, while discussed and considered, never came anywhere close to being put into action, and remained an obscure historical footnote.

While the territory does start as a minor nation, control of Singapore could be vital for dominance in the Asia-Pacific region due to its highly strategic location in addition to being a choke point, something that eventually becomes apparent once
expands as part of their plans for a Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere .
The flag used in the game is identical of the former Straits Settlements, which had Singapore as its capital.

The first European outposts in the region were established by the Dutch in the 17th century. The British occupied these during the Napoleonic wars, and confirmed their control through a treaty with the Netherlands in 1824, which formally separated Malaya from the
. Initially limited to Singapore and a few other trading centers known as the Straits Settlements, in the late 19th century British rule expanded over the whole peninsula via protectorates.

British dominance over the Malay peninsula was of vital interest to the Empire, due to its abundant resources as well as Singapore's strategic location at the southern end of the Straits of Malacca, the most direct passage between the Indian and Pacific Oceans to the west and east respectively.

's idea of a Greater East Asian Co-Prosperity Sphere , they invaded Malaya and Singapore in December 1941. At the time, Singapore was the foremost British military base and economic port in the region. The swift fall of Singapore in February 1942, thought to be well-defended, was one of the greatest British setbacks in the Pacific theater and was called the "worst disaster" in British military history by Winston Churchill. The Japanese renamed the city to Syonan-to and occupied it until the end of the war with its surrender in August 1945.

Following the war, Malaya and Singapore returned to the British, this time with increased autonomy. After the return of the British, there were growing nationalist sentiment amongst the local populace, as many felt that the British were no longer competent in their administration and defence of the crown colony and its inhabitants. It became independent in 1957 and merged with Singapore, British North Borneo and Sarawak to form Malaysia in 1963. Singapore was expelled from Malaysia in 1965 and became its own sovereign nation.

The fascist route for Liberia is definitely a route to consider, as the generic fascist branch in the focus tree will give you an extra 7 percent recruitable manpower, which is a much-needed bonus for a small country like Liberia with its tiny population. However, going fascist also means that you will be surrounded by a hostile
that can easily crush you, so keep that in mind. Still, if played well, a fascist Liberia may well one day be able to control the entire African continent.

The first thing to do in order to get on the route to African domination is to take the Political Effort focus, which will give you an extra 120 political power. Use this political power to hire Ebenezer Cailloux, who will give you 0.10 fascist support per day. Hiring him will also unlock the "Fascism on the rise" decisions, where you can decide to either fire a civil war or switch to fascism peacefully in a referendum. If you want to do the civil war, remember to disband your one division, as once the civil war starts the division will most likely go to the enemy's side. Then, make an infantry division with one cavalry unit, train it, and deploy it to quickly take your opponent's victory points.

While you wait to turn fascist, use your one civilian factory to build some more civs, and take your industrial focuses to get some free civilian and military factories, which will be very valuable, since Liberia has next-to-none starting factories. Once you finish turning fascist, you can now progress down the rest of your political focuses to get that extra recruitable population. Also, at this point you should have researched Basic Machine Tools, Dispersed/Concentrated Industry, Construction One, as well as some Electronics techs to boost research speed and maybe some Infantry techs to boost soft attack. Artillery is highly recommended but probably not feasible given Liberia's limited research slots- so is Close Air Support. Try to fit these in if you can. Your political power, should also be spent first on getting to war economy for 150 political power, then take some Improved Worker Conditions, Anti-Democratic/Communist Raids to get your stability up, and then if you have enough political power, a Captain of Industry. At this point, it should be around late 1938, to mid 1939, and here you can make a decision. Either you can join the Axis and use your limited army to quickly grab some Allied land- or you can build up your army and industry, wait for the Allies to pull their troops out of Africa, and

strike. Both are feasible, but this guide will focus on you waiting. But if you want to quickly attack, go ahead- it will mostly be a game of cat-and-mouse for you, since your units will melt when faced with any Allied troops, so your main focus will be shifting your units around to pin down as much enemy troops as you can as you wait for Germany and Italy to come to your rescue.

Now, if you decide to wait, then your focus should be building up an elite army made up of small, quick, and flexible special forces units- marines, or mountaineers work well. A standard 10 width of marines/mountaineers, with support artillery, support anti-aircraft, support anti-tank, engineers, and field hospitals to conserve your precious manpower. Train as much of these as you can, exercise them until they're regulars, and then strike. If at this point France has not capitulated yet, then quickly grab some of their territory as it's highly likely they won't have any units stationed there. Also take some of Great Britain's land as well. Once France has capitulated, your job will be to support the Germans ad Italians in pushing the British out of North Africa.
Once the Brits and French have been kicked out of North Africa, turn your attention to

Africa, which if not capitulated, will most likely be duking it out with the Italians in Central and East Africa- send your units here, as the Italians aren't too reliable. By this time, if you have Service by Requirement or higher, you'll be able to field at least 11 divisions of special forces- put these to good use in pushing the South Africans. This will also give you some extra warscore to take some more British and French African territories in the peace conference. With Africa firmly in Axis hands, Britain should fall quickly as well. Take their African land, and there you have it. A much more powerful and bigger Liberia.

The sheikhdom became a British protectorate between 1899 and 1961 following the Anglo-Kuwaiti agreement of 1899. This agreement was made between Sheikh Mubarak Al-Sabah and the British Government in India, primarily as a defensive measure against threats from the Ottoman Empire.

Throughout the 1930s, Kuwaiti people opposed the British imposed separation of Kuwait from Iraq. In 1938, the "Free Kuwaiti Movement" was established by Kuwaiti youth who opposed British rule and submitted a petition requesting the Iraqi government reunifies Kuwait and Iraq. Due to fears of armed uprising in Kuwait, the Al Sabah agreed to the establishment of a legislative council to represent the "Free Kuwaiti Movement" demanding the reunification of Iraq and Kuwait. The council's first meeting in 1938 resulted in unanimous resolutions demanding the reunification of Kuwait and Iraq.
On 22 February 1938, oil was first discovered in the Burgan field.

In March 1939, a popular armed uprising erupted within Kuwait to reunify with Iraq. The Al Sabah family, along with British military support, violently put down the uprising, and killed and imprisoned its participants.[118] King Ghazi of Iraq publicly demanded the release of the Kuwaiti prisoners and warned the Al Sabah family to end the repression of the "Free Kuwaiti Movement".

Latvia achieved independence as a result of the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, signed between Imperial Germany, Austria-Hungary and the Russian Provisional Government in March 1918. After the collapse of the Russian Provisional government and the rise of the Bolshevik communist regime, the Petrograd Soviet, seeking to prevent Baltic independence and spread the proletarian world revolution, invaded the Baltic region. Latvia joined forces with the rest of the Baltic States to defend its independence and was able to stop the Russian offensive. A peace treaty was signed in 1920 and Latvia's independence was recognized by the rest of the world after World War I. As part of the secret protocol of the Molotov-Ribbentrop pact, Eastern Europe was divided into spheres of interest by

. Latvia was in the Soviet zone and was occupied by the Soviet Union in 1940. This occupation was briefly interrupted in 1941 by Operation Barbarossa when Germany occupied the area, reorganizing the Baltic States into the "Reichskommisariat Ostland". The area was re-occupied by the Soviet Union in 1944-1945 and the Baltic States were annexed into the Soviet Union after the end of World War II and reorganized into the Estonian SSR, Latvian SSR and Lithuanian SSR. Latvia remained part of the Soviet Union until 1991 when it declared itself independent during the collapse of the Soviet Union.

Shandong's return to Chinese administration came during the Warlord Era of the Republic of China, when the Zhili clique of warlords was given control, but after the Second Zhili–Fengtian War of 1924, the northeast China-based Fengtian clique took over. In April 1925, the Fengtian clique installed the warlord Zhang Zongchang, nicknamed the "Dogmeat General", as military governor of Shandong Province. Time dubbed him China's "basest warlord". He ruled over the province until 1928 when he was ousted in the wake of the Northern Expedition. He was succeeded by Han Fuju, who was loyal to the warlord Feng Yuxiang but later switched his allegiance to the Nanjing government headed by Chiang Kai-shek. Han Fuju also ousted the warlord Liu Zhennian, nicknamed the "King of Shandong East", who ruled eastern Shandong Province, hence unifying the province under his rule.

In 1937 Japan began its invasion of China in the Second World War, which would eventually become part of the Pacific theater. Han Fuju was made Deputy Commander in Chief of the 5th War Area and put in charge of defending the lower Yellow River valley. However, he abandoned his base and about 600,000 Ethnic Chinese civilians fled out Jinan city with only elderly too old to leave remaining when Japanese troops crossed the Yellow River.

Surviving the inevitable war with Italy is possible, and can lead to the player going into WW2 with a very capable and elite fighting force. First you must withdraw your small starting army to your capital in the mountains as trying to defend in the desert will lead to equipment and manpower losses that you can not absorb. Your industry is non existent, with only a single military factory and no civilian factories. Take the military focus path beginning with "The Afar Armed Forces" for 35 days and once complete use the army XP to add four units of regular infantry to the irregulars template to bring it up to 16 width while also buffing the stats. Use the last 5 XP to add the infantry equipment MIO to your rifle design or paint over one of the irregular battalions with regular infantry in the division template, whichever you prefer. Use your first 50 pp to appoint the defensive chief of army and make sure everyone is dug in with max entrenchment, appoint your field marshal, give him the defensive trait as soon as the cp becomes available, and either charismatic or org first, again, your choice, as second trait. Once Italy sends you the ultimatum, reject, obviously, and after a day or two they will war dec you. Don't try to attack, your divisions will be under strength but if you stay dug in and rely on the entrenchment bonus you will lose very little material and manpower to Italy's attacks and can begin to build up. At this point it's simply up to you to manage the various aspects of the ongoing defense. Build more units and follow the army focus path taking the right hand branch to max out your manpower, conscription laws, free military factories and some free infantry units. You should be able to build around ten to twelve units of infantry throughout the Italian war, research mountaineers and paint over the irregulars in your division template with mountaineers or regular infantry. Use last stand only if things get bad, if you focus on building up and improving your division template, and number of divisions, you should never be in any real danger and can often take out ~400k Italians for 4-5k of your own people.

If you survive this, join the allies once Germany declares war on Poland and watch the British push the Italians out of Ethiopia, you can help if you want to speed things along but be careful not to over reach. Once Ethiopia is liberated you can send your now very elite army off anywhere you feel like helping out however until Vichy France joins the war you wont be able to get any naval bases. Your options are somewhat limited and Axis submarines combined with not having many transports make it hard to move around but you can still help out and have some fun. Keep one or two divisions at home as Vichy France just seems to join at random and can march straight into your capital. Eventually Ethiopia will leave the Allies and make their own Faction so if you want to take them out I'd advise getting the focus that gives you a war goal on them as it doesn't run out so it's handy to have for when you want it. If you use the war goal as soon as they flip the invasion will be very easy however it can become almost impossible if you let Ethiopia build up again. Do not invite any allies as they will always get a higher war score and steal some land, making the consolidate the Horn of Africa decision impossible.

Throughout the colonial era, many Indians arrived as soldiers, civil servants, construction workers and traders and, along with the Anglo-Burmese community, dominated commercial and civil life in Burma. Rangoon became the capital of British Burma and an important port between Calcutta and Singapore. Burmese resentment was strong, and was vented in violent riots that periodically paralysed Rangoon until the 1930s. Some of the discontent was caused by a disrespect for Burmese culture and traditions. Buddhist monks became the vanguards of the independence movement. U Wisara, an activist monk, died in prison after a 166-day hunger strike. On 1 April 1937, Burma became a separately administered colony of Britain, and Ba Maw became the first Prime Minister and Premier of Burma. Ba Maw was an outspoken advocate for Burmese self-rule, and he opposed the participation of Britain, and by extension Burma, in World War II. He resigned from the Legislative Assembly and was arrested for sedition. In 1940, before Japan formally entered the war, Aung San formed the Burma Independence Army in Japan.

As a major battleground, Burma was devastated during World War II by the Japanese invasion. Within months after they entered the war, Japanese troops had advanced on Rangoon, and the British administration had collapsed. A Burmese Executive Administration headed by Ba Maw was established by the Japanese in August 1942. Wingate's British Chindits were formed into long-range penetration groups trained to operate deep behind Japanese lines. A similar American unit, Merrill's Marauders, followed the Chindits into the Burmese jungle in 1943. Beginning in late 1944, allied troops launched a series of offensives that led to the end of Japanese rule in July 1945. The battles were intense with much of Burma laid waste by the fighting. Overall, the Japanese lost some 150,000 men in Burma with 1,700 prisoners taken. Although many Burmese fought initially for the Japanese as part of the Burma Independence Army, many Burmese, mostly from the ethnic minorities, served in the British Burma Army. The Burma National Army and the Arakan National Army fought with the Japanese from 1942 to 1944 but switched allegiance to the Allied side in 1945.

It's no secret that Burma starts in a pretty bad position with one civilian industry, but given some smart moves and cheese you should be able to form a pretty formidable Burma, given some time, effort, and luck. With a big population similar to Siam and the large amount of tungsten, it can make up for a good trade option with the Allies. Unlike Siam, Burma does not possess a formable nation option

Now, the first thing you should do is take the first Political focus, which will give you 120 political power, plus the 70 you have already accumulated. Use this to get a fascist advisor. Yes, I know, going fascist is the go-to strategy for basically every minor, but if it works, it works. While you wait for fascist support to tick up, take some industrial focuses to get some free factories. Grab the two free civilian factories first, then get the three military factories. By this time you should be above fifty percent fascist support, so hold a referendum to become State of Burma. Use your excess political power to get war economy, and if you have any extra left, get some Improved Worker Conditions or Anti-Communist/Democratic raids. You can join Japan to assist with their invasions. Otherwise, if your manpower is still an issue you can go communist to get to the weekly manpower army experience.

By now you should have a total of 4 or 5 factories- 2 civilian and 3 military. One of your civilian factories will be used for consumer goods, so use the remaining one to either build some more civs or trade for some steel. Use one of your 3 military factories to produce artillery, and use the other 2 to build guns. Set some factories to build support equipment as well once you get some more mils.

At this point, you should've flipped fascist already, so start justifying on Laos. At the same time start working on the political focuses. Make a template of one cavalry unit, and spam it out. You should also have a fair amount of political power at this point, so take some stability-increasing decisions. Should you declare on Siam, Cambodia, Vietnam or Malaysia and win against them each other can give you enough expansion and access to some valuable resources and sea access.

Shanxi starts off with 2 debuffs on political power and stability. Choose Secure Internal Politics to get a fascist demagogue and complete Industrial Investment, Local Arms Production, Public Education Reform and finally Opposition before fire off a civil war.

Keep training your starting army until you get 5 Army EXP to make a cavalry unit. To prepare for civil war, queue a cavalry division and remember to lower your stability from time to time with the decision to Commandeer Civilian Trains and Prepare for Civil War. Delete your starting army before the civil war.

When the civil war has started, force deploy the cavalry unit to start capturing victory point and after the civil war, you're now fascist with no debuffs spirit. Then, you have to join Japan's faction once its available and build yourself up for the border wars without any threats from anyone, just don't join Japan's war. Focus on the other warlords' territories like Xibei San Ma and Sinkiang since the supply is horrendous there. Your faction members will flood their army in so turn off the supply sharing to only supply yourself.

As for the border conflict template, 6 divisions of 7-2 is good enough with your limited industry. Research mountaineer is a good start as well. If you have extra military factories, you might want to add in support artillery, medium flame tank, engineer, radio and recon company. Don't border war with Communist China and Nationalist China initially. To win the border war with Communist China, you have to place your army at Ordos border with Shaanxi which controlled by Communist China to start the conflict.

When you get enough land, industry and army, you can consider to leave Japan's faction and let them declare war on you since they have a wargoal on you that stays with them even after they lost to the Allies.

There are 2 focus you can get in the end of Opposition path: Nationalist or Communist. If you decide to go for Nationalist China focus tree, immediately Invite Foreign Investor and rush down all the focus on the German side to get the buffs for your army and extra military factories. With that, you can build up even stronger than before. Then, the future of Shanxi is depends on your choice.

However, if you decided to go for Communist China focus tree, kick out the fascist demagogue during civil war. Wait till you get enough PP to get a Communist Revolutionary and flip to Communist as Shanxi Soviet Republic. You have to wait till your Communist ideology reaches 50% to get the Communist focus tree in Proclaim The Rival Government. Then you have to rush Social Democracy path to annex China peacefully, collect all their troops and prepare to rush down Guangxi Clique as they are the faction leader. Since you're in Japan's faction, they will give you back your core territories. If everything is done right, the China War should end in 1940 and you have time to prep yourself before leaving the faction and let Japan declare war on you.

Alternately, you can hire a fascist demagogue after Secure Internal Politics and remove your debuffs in Cooperation with the Nationalist. You need to keep increasing the fascist ideology through decision and events to hopefully turn fascist before the China War, stop taking any focus to gain more Political Power if necessary. After joined Japan's faction, do the same thing by annex China peacefully, rush down Guangxi and reclaim all of China.

. Operations all require at least one agent to perform, and many require more than one, with some powerful ones requiring three operatives, which is more than what a country can have without any additional bonuses. They also all need some level of network to have been built up in preparation.
Operations all need preparation before they can be launched. This is usually produced

, agents, or a cost in industry over time. Once preparation is done, an operation can have multiple phases. The most common is to have three phases: infiltration, performing the job, and exfiltration.
The success of the operations is depending on your

, your network strength in the Country and the general risk of the operation. Different Operations have different base classifications: some are very likely to success, while others are very risky. Plant False Intelligence has 0% risk, but instead it has high prerequisites to become available. Infiltration, Making Resistance Contacts, Preparing a Collaboration Government, and Rescue operations have a low risk of 10%. Capture Cipher, Stealing Blueprints, Strengthen Resistance, and Sabotage operations have a medium risk of 20%. Orchestrate Coup and Coordinated Strike have a high risk of 30%.
Each operation has 3 phases: an infiltration, an execution, and an exfiltration. Each of these phases are randomly chosen, with modifiers depending on technology,

. Each random phase rolled has different cost requirements. The sum of costs of these phases determines the total operation cost, unless the operation has already been conducted, at which point the operation cost can scale. Each operation rolls from the same infiltration and exfiltration phases, but execution phases are operation-specific.

The "Plant False Intelligence" Operation does not have Infiltration and Exfiltration phases, but rather a combination of 3 distinct Execution phases. The "Orchestrate Coup" and "Coordinated Strike" Operations do not have an Exfiltration Phase, but rather an additional Execution Phase.

Overview of the Second Philippine Republic
The invasion of the Philippine islands and government creation

is an archipelagic country in Southeast Asia, and is a strategic location for naval invasions. Through a Japanese decision, the Second Philippine Republic can be released depending on how many lands that Japan can occupy from the ongoing war with the East and Southeast Asian nations or if they are annexed.

After the Japanese invasion of the Philippines, President Manuel L. Quezon had declared the national capital Manila an "open city", and left it under the rule of Jorge B. Vargas, as mayor. The Japanese entered the city on January 2, 1942, and established it as the capital. Japan fully captured the Philippines on May 6, 1942, after the Battle of Corregidor. On September 21, 1944, Laurel placed the Republic under martial law. On September 23, 1944, the Republic officially declared war against the United States and United Kingdom. Following the return of American-led Allied forces, the government of the Second Republic evacuated Manila to Baguio. The republic was formally dissolved by Laurel in Tokyo on August 17, 1945 – two days after the surrender of Japan.
The "Capture of Manila" event triggers when Manila is taken by an invading force, Japan can take the decision to release the Second Philippine Republic as a Japanese puppet.
The Second Philippine Republic starts with 2 research slots, and can gain 3 more slots from its national focuses.

In order to play as early as the Second Philippine Republic , is to play first as Japan and continue the war with China as soon as possible in the 1939 scenario. In this case, just invade and occupy China before preparing yourself to fight against USA for the war. Considering that the Philippines are owned as a colony by the USA. But, if the Philippines has capitulated and is in faction with anyone else, then Japan can take the 'Establish the Second Philippine Republic' decision, thus finally releasing the PSR.

In a matter of technology, PSR also inherits whatever the Philippines or Japan gain from national focuses or by decision, if the player wishes to remain to play as Japan a little longer just to have their technologies passable for the puppet state, PSR gets them altogether. is a releasable country in the
region of Carpathian Ruthenia. It can be released via a focus. It cannot be released manually, but can be released in a peace deal if its cores still exist.

20 years earlier, by the 1920 Treaty of Trianon, the region, which had historically belonged to Hungary, had been detached from the Kingdom of Hungary and attached to newly created Czechoslovakia. Subsequently Hungary had sought revision of the Treaty of Trianon and the restoration of her historical borders.
On 2 November 1938 the First Vienna Award separated territories from Czechoslovakia, including southern Carpathian Rus', that were mostly Hungarian-populated and returned them to Hungary.
After the breakup of the Second Czechoslovak Republic, Carpatho-Ukraine on 15 March 1939 proclaimed itself an independent republic, headed by President Avgustyn Voloshyn.

However, Nazi Germany sided with Hungary against Ukrainian independence, and the short-lived state was invaded by the Kingdom of Hungary and Poland, crushing all local resistance by 18 March 1939. The region remained under Hungarian control until the end of World War II in Europe, after which it was occupied and annexed by the Soviet Union. The territory is now administered as the Ukrainian Zakarpattia Oblast.

At the beginning of the 20th century, the Ottoman Empire had control over most of the Arabian peninsula. Subject to this suzerainty, Arabia was ruled by a patchwork of tribal rulers, with the Sharif of Mecca having pre-eminence and ruling the Hejaz and the Al Rashid Family ruling in Nejd but with the Al Saud family fighting to take control over Nejd. In 1916, with the encouragement and support of Britain , the Sharif of Mecca, Hussein bin Ali, led a pan-Arab revolt against the Ottoman Empire to create a united Arab state. Although the Arab Revolt of 1916 to 1918 failed in its objective, the Allied victory in World War I resulted in the end of Ottoman suzerainty and control in Arabia.

The Al Saud avoided involvement in the Arab Revolt, and instead continued their struggle with the Al Rashid. Following the latter's final defeat, he took the title Sultan of Nejd in 1921. With the help of the Ikhwan, a tribal army inspired by Wahhabism and led by Faisal Al-Dawish, the Hejaz was conquered in 1924–25 and on 10 January 1926, Ibn Saud declared himself King of the Hejaz. A year later, he added the title of King of Nejd. For the next five years, he administered the two parts of his dual kingdom as separate units. In 1932 the two kingdoms of the Hejaz and Nejd were united as the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

The new kingdom was one of the poorest countries in the world, reliant on limited agriculture and pilgrimage revenues. In 1938, vast reserves of oil were discovered in the Al-Ahsa region along the coast of the Persian Gulf, and full-scale development of the oil fields began in 1941 under the US-controlled Aramco . Oil provided Saudi Arabia with economic prosperity and substantial political leverage internationally.

Saudi Arabia severed diplomatic contacts with Germany on 11 September 1939, and with Japan in October 1941. Although officially neutral, the Saudis provided the Allies with large supplies of oil. Diplomatic relations with the United States were established in 1943. King Abdul Aziz Al-Saud was a personal friend of Franklin D. Roosevelt. The Americans were then allowed to build an air force base near Dhahran. On 28 February 1945, Saudi Arabia declared war on Germany and Japan, but no military actions resulted from the declaration.

A small population, lack of resource, besides oil, as well as behind technology would represent a big problem for Saudi Arabia. In order to even have a possible chance to form Arabia, the United Kingdom must have gone to the decolonization focus branch in which Britain need to give back Aden to Yemen, as well as release most of its possessions in the Middle East and North Africa, including Sudan. By this way, Saudi Arabia would have a slightly higher chance than Iraq to form the supposed major nation, but more enough than the rest of the Arab states. If the custom difficulty of Decolonized Africa and Asia, Saudi Arabia has an open way to conquer and annex all of North Africa, excluding South Sudan and Western Sahara, having the chance to form Arabia. Saudi Arabia has a choice in it's political branch: Manpower and fascism, Political power and communism and Nonaligned status quo.

One of the better option would be to increase the quality of each division. Research towards artillery and equipment would be needed. It is also optional to mechanize since there wouldn't be a lack of oil, at least for Arabian consumption. The first target would be Yemen since conquering Oman first would overstretch Saudi strength. After carefully pushing and defeating Yemen, it's advisable to puppet them for what manpower you can still use of them. And, if feeling lucky, you can annex them instead of puppeting.

You can then take over Iraq and puppet them as well for manpower. Iraq and Turkey would be a great obstacle for Saudi Arabia. Out of the two, Iraq is the weaker of the two, not only of their population, but also a small army and no navy. It is critical that the player strike quickly before Iran mobilize. If they muster a strong army, the best and perhaps only option would be to make a frontline around the Iraqi river in the south and north Iraq and some divisions in the center to prevent Baghdad to be under Iranian hands. Once Iran is defeated, only Turkey would be a serious block. By that moment, the player would have exploited the Middle Eastern manpower.

Following the Spanish-American war of 1898,
was not annexed by the

in the Treaty of Paris unlike the other Spanish possessions of the Philippines or Puerto Rico. Instead it gained independence as a sovereign state due to the Teller Amendment passed by the US Congress that same year. Nonetheless, the American occupiers stayed until independence was granted in 1902.
remained heavily influenced by the

, tariffs were cut, and the economy became dominated by their northern neighbor - 4 years after the war American companies owned 80% of Cuban ore exports along with most of the sugar and tobacco factories. Moreover, the

joined the Great War as a member of the Entente but their participation was more about moral support than anything else acting as a base against German U-boats in the Caribbean and a further 100 qualified doctors were sent to the western front. After the war, in 1925, president Gerardo Machado was elected and a period of modernization began with the Carretera Central being built which was a highway that crossed the entire island. Machado, however, stayed longer than his term but slowly through concessions to the opposition, the balance of power changed yet again and shortly after Machado's fall from power in the summer of 1933 both a general strike and a coup took place led by protesting students, and non-commissioned military officers, labor activists and the likes.

After the 1933 Cuban revolution it was decided that Ramón Grau would become the next president - he was an ardent opponent of Machado's regime and jailed for it in 1931. Grau's regime became known as the 'Hundred Days Government' and in this time a law was passed declaring that half of all workers in agriculture, commerce and industry had to be Cuban citizens greatly undermining foreign influence, at the dismay of the
. Furthermore, a minimum wage was established and women obtained the right to vote among countless other reforms. This was hailed as the first time that
was governed by Cubans. Then in 1934 an anti-government coalition backed by the

made up of right-wing civilian and military elements toppled the liberal government. The military requested Carlos Hevia to come to power, his rule lasted less than a week, and set in motion a period of interim presidents. José Agripino Barnet became president in December 1935 and with the looming 1936 elections on the horizon its clear change is too come.
